This not only provides a new strategy for the sustainable development of Salvia miltiorrhiza but also suggests that this method can be applied to the production of other medicinal components.
igem_OTIA-Hangzhou_2024: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are toxic byproducts of oxygen metabolism and a major cause of skin aging. The skin has a natural defense system to eliminate ROS, but as we age and with increased UV exposure, these protective substances diminish, allowing more free radicals to accumulate and cause cellular damage. Studies have shown that neoagarooligosaccharides (NAOS) possess antioxidant properties and can effectively inhibit excess ROS. Our project involves designing an E. coli prokaryotic expression system to produce β-agarase (AgaA), an enzyme that specifically cleaves the β-1,4 glycosidic bond between D-galactose and 3,6-anhydro-α-L-galactose residues in agarose, generating the antioxidant NAOS. Using the ABTS method, we confirmed the antioxidant capability of NAOS. This antioxidant can be incorporated into skincare products to eliminate excess ROS in the skin, thereby protecting skin health.
igem_BGI-MammothEdu-East_2024: Scentinel is an innovative project that harnesses synthetic biology to produce aromatic compounds aimed at improving the lives of visually impaired women. The name "Scentinel" combines "scent" and "sentinel," symbolizing how our fragrance-based solutions act as a guardian for women’s health, particularly during their menstrual periods. By engineering yeast to biosynthesize terpenes like limonene and nerol, we develop products that emit specific scents, helping women detect the onset of their menstrual periods. This empowers them to manage their menstrual health with greater independence and dignity. Additionally, our products include fragrances designed to alleviate anxiety and stress during menstruation, along with antimicrobial properties to ensure hygiene. Through this project, we aim to combine science and empathy, creating solutions that address both physiological and emotional needs, ultimately enhancing the quality of life for this underserved community.
igem_BGI-MammothEdu-South_2024: Anxiety disrupts the ability to relax, leading to difficulties in falling asleep. Traditional night lights, which many rely on for comfort. Exposure to light before bed can suppress melatonin levels, making it harder to fall asleep. PetalGlow was designed to offer a unique and holistic approach to mental well-being. At daytime, PetalGlow incorporates the therapeutic benefits of horticultural therapy. It arrives as a young plant, ready to grow under your care. Daily tasks like watering and caring for PetalGlow's growth create a mindful routine that alleviates mild anxiety and stress, promotes relaxation, and enhances mood. As night falls, PetalGlow takes its therapeutic effects a step further by emitting a soft, calming bioluminescent light that creates an ideal pre-sleep environment. Unlike harsh night lights, PetalGlow’s subtle glow provides just enough illumination to ease you into a restful state without disrupting the darkness needed for sleep.
igem_Sorbonne-U-Paris_2024: Morpheus project aims to tackle the degradation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into bioproducts yielding high industrial value, in order to address the pressing plastic crisis in today’s world. To achieve this, our objective is to create a mutant strain of a single-cell algae, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, competent to bioconvert PET into terpenes, specifically vanillic acid, for its appealing use in satisfaction of the rising demand of various end-use industries. The biodegradation pathway involving these enzymes has already been discovered in the bacterium Ideonella sakaiensis. However, our innovative approach consists of integrating this pathway in a green component of the natural cycle, by a transformation process with a plasmid constructed by us containing the fusion protein of PETase-MHETase enzymes. This step is followed by the conversion of the product of terephthalic acid (TPA) to vanillic acid, leaving a byproduct of ethylene glycol (EG), lucrative for industrial and pharmaceutical uses.
igem_SCU-China_2024: The high chlorogenic acid accumulation in Nicotiana benthamiana limits its potential for synthesizing other products. To develop tobacco as a versatile chassis for the short-term, efficient synthesis of desired plant natural products, we first constructed a genome-scale metabolic model (GSMM) and used COBRA algorithms to formulate the best metabolic flow adjustment strategies. Subsequently, the critical gene NbHQTs for chlorogenic acid synthesis in tobacco was knocked out using CRISPR/Cas9, and a low chlorogenic acid level tobacco chassis was obtained. We then introduced heterologous synthetic pathways for phaselic acid, resveratrol, and crocin into the chassis and improved the synthesis capability by engineered critical enzymes. The chassis could quickly synthesize the desired functional products to fulfill different requirements and is expected to be developed into an efficient biological reactor for the biopharmaceutical industry, thereby promoting the green transformation and upgrading of the traditional tobacco cultivation industry.
igem_SCUT-China-A_2024: In an endeavor to mitigate the escalating crisis of global carbon dioxide emissions, we have engineered Halomonas TD, a salt-resistant microorganism, to efficiently synthesize multiple bioproducts from carbon dioxide-derived electrolyte(CDE), which primarily consisting of acetate. In the course of our project, we have incorporated the formate assimilation pathway and enhanced TD's tolerance to acetate through adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE), thereby augmenting the conversion rate. Owing to the absence of efficient dynamic control tools in TD, we have constructed a thermosensitive bio-switch (T-switch) tailored to its requirements. By leveraging the modified TD, we have successfully achieved the production of P34HB, Tyrian purple, SOD, and PhaP. To address the issue of high-density induction failure encountered during large-scale production, we have developed a fermentation model capable of real-time feeding. Concurrently, we have also created a software application for genome neutral locus screening, which has been seamlessly integrated into our project.
igem_REC-CHENNAI_2024: Microplastic pollution is a global threat. Humans, on average, are exposed to 2012 ± 598 microplastic particles, through ingestion, inhalation, or dermal contact, causing serious health issues like reproductive abnormalities, oxidative stress and neurotoxicity. To address this issue, we propose a three-stage solution utilising the affinity between peptides and microplastics: modeling, expression and deployment. Interaction between shortlisted peptides and microplastic particles were studied using molecular dynamics. The most efficient peptide’s sequence was cloned into expression host E.coli BL21(DE3). The recombinant peptides, containing hexa histidine tags bind strongly to Ni-NTA affinity resins. The his-tags aided purification and in deployment. The resin-peptide complex efficiently captures hydrophobic microplastics upon contact. Microscopic and spectrofluorimetric analyses of the recovered resin-peptide complex would demonstrate the successful removal of microplastics from the test sample. This method is simple, avoids harmful chemicals, and works under various conditions.
igem_UBC-Vancouver_2024: As global demand for data storage skyrockets, studies report that traditional data centres are projected to be incapable of meeting the demands of the near future. They also cause environmental damage by depleting natural resources. nuCloud is a synthetic biology-based DNA data storage platform that addresses the unmet demand for global data storage. Inspired by the high storage density, durability, and efficiency of DNA, nuCloud offers a solid-phase enzymatic DNA synthesis system using a thermostable TdT variant. Combined with an automated microfluidic system and error-correcting software pipeline, nuCloud can encode digital information into nucleotide sequences, synthesize corresponding DNA strands, and decode it back to binaries for its users. This innovative approach provides a sustainable and scalable biomanufacturing solution to meet the data storage demands of the future.
igem_UToronto_2024: This year at iGEM Toronto, we are developing Plasmid.AI – a platform that uses generative AI to create new, functional DNA sequences. Our ultimate goal is to write entirely new genomes to create novel organisms that have fine-tuned phenotypes. To make headway towards this challenging task, we are starting with the simplest proof of concept – the generation and validation of new plasmid components. To do this, our dry lab team employs sequence-based machine learning approaches to generate novel plasmid sequences. Key plasmid components, such as the origin of replication, are generated and validated in silico. The wet lab team then assesses the viability of these components in vitro – the results of these assays refining dry lab’s next iteration of sequences. Concurrently, the hardware team develops high-throughput tools for automated plasmid testing, supported by a comprehensive human practices education campaign and entrepreneurship initiatives to bring AI-driven solutions to market.
igem_PekingHSC_2024: Cancer is a major global public health issue. Bacterial therapy has attracted much attention due to its ability to colonize and proliferate specifically in the tumor microenvironment (TME). As an amyloid protein, CsgA can be secreted and form fiber structure on the surface of E. coli. By combining Genetic Code Expansion (GCE) technology, we tried to insert the Unnatural Amino Acid (UAA) Tet v2.0 into CsgA. In the principle of click chemistry, prodrug TCO-Dox would site-specific release in the TME, thus effectively killing tumor cells. With the potential to improve efficacy and reduce side effects, this innovative strategy provides new possibilities for cancer treatment.
igem_UTokyo_2024: If your vision changes, your life will change. Glaucoma is a serious eye disease that can affect anyone. Even with modern medical technology, there is no cure for the disease, and the purpose of treatments is only to slow its progression. Late detection renders treatment delay, leading to a decline in QOV (Quality of Vision) with symptoms such as blurred decreasing vision, and even blindness. POIROT is aimed to detect glaucoma biomarker miRNA easily at home. We adopted a protein-based cell-free system to achieve rapid social implementation. The series of reactions proceeds isothermally, and test results can be visually determined by color changes, with useability emphasized. Furthermore, POIROT has potential applications for other diseases, as it can efficiently quantify disease-specific (tiny amounts) nucleic acids in body fluids.
igem_HUST-UEVE-UPSaclay_2024: The main aim of our project is to degrade PET and double enrich the degradation product TPA. We first use engineered E. coli BL21 strain to secrete turboPETase. After that, another engineered E. coli BL21 strain is responsible for enriching TPA and indicating the level of enrichment by expressing fluorescence after it transports TPA into itself. Next, we use C. elegans, a model organism that feeds on E. coli, as our recycler and amplifier. After two engineered E. coli BL21 strain have achieved the expected processing of PET and absorption of TPA, we introduce the C. elegans that feed on the engineered bacteria to avoid biological leakage, then further achieve the goal of enrichment and recycling. Meanwhile, the engineering of C. elegans is ongoing-we are attempting to create a kind of C. elegans with the ability to transport TPA into their intestinal cell, in order to further enrich TPA monomers.
igem_BWYA_2024: Our project, Luna Pad, addresses the critical issue of late diagnoses of gynecological diseases by transforming menstrual pads into non-invasive screening tools. Integrating test strips that utilize lateral flow assay technology, the pads detect biomarkers such as CA126 and IL-6, indicative of inflammations and cancers. We adopted single-chain variable fragment (scFv) antibodies designs for improved synthesis in E. coli. Designed for ease of use and affordability, the Luna Pad aims to encourage regular health monitoring and early detection, potentially saving lives by prompting necessary medical interventions.
igem_SHSBNU-China_2024: Project STAR is targeted at anxiety among high school students and the global population by harnessing L-theanine, a naturally occurring amino acid in tea leaves. To overcome the limitations in traditional synthesis methods, we developed a de novo synthetic biology approach to produce L-theanine in E. coli BL21. We've designed a pathway involving five enzymes to synthesize L-theanine starting from glucose with an ATP regeneration system for efficiency. We investigated the implementation of the product as candies, and explored delivery methods. We expanded the scope of our care via community events of promoting anxiety awareness.
igem_BASIS-China_2024: Microplastic particles are not only posing a threat to the ecosystem but also invisibly infiltrating our daily lives. In our efforts, we decided to focus on degrading microplastics using PETase. With the help of AI tools, we successfully designed and constructed sequences of PETase that efficiently degrade PET. To have a sustainable production of the enzymes, we further introduced these sequences into cyanobacteria. The cyanobacteria are then placed in bioreactors alongside rhodobacteria, creating a system capable of breaking down microplastics more effectively and sufficiently. Alongside the achievements within the lab, we also organized a range of different human practice events to support our program development and guide our experiments while conveying our core value and raising public awareness about this invisible threat.
igem_Heidelberg_2024: Cells interpret identical DNA sequences differently depending on the 3D genome organization, leading to diverse cellular phenotypes and even determining between health and disease. While synthetic biology provides powerful methods to engineer the genome sequence, tools to sculpt the genome's spatial architecture are lacking. We address this profound gap by introducing PICasSO, a toolbox for rationally engineering the 3D genome organization. Using different CRISPR/Cas orthologs and new, engineered fusion guide RNAs, we created "Cas staples" that bind and connect otherwise non-interacting genomic regions. To streamline the development cycle of new Cas staples, we developed DaVinci, a multi-faceted model integrating both local and long-range DNA-protein interactions into a unified pipeline. Combining PICasSO and DaVinci, we recapitulated mechanistic core principles of enhancer hijacking - a driver of tumor development. Our comprehensive part collection and extensive education program enable the next generation of iGEMers to efficiently adapt PICasSO and engineer genomes in 3D.
igem_NJMU-CHINA_2024: In the present study,  we engineered probiotics to produce small molecules for treating depression and Alzheimer's disease. For depression, utilizing molecular docking and SPR, we identified inosine as a molecule capable of decoupling SERT-nNOS. We engineered Lactobacillus plantarum L168 to produce inosine by incorporating the key enzyme gsk. The engineered probiotics release inosine in the gut, which then travels through the bloodstream to the brain, disconnecting SERT from nNOS to alleviate depressive symptoms. Regarding Alzheimer's disease，we identified tetrahydrofolate as an effective LilrB3 binder and  produce it using the key enzyme sequence folKE. Tetrahydrofolate binds to LilrB3 receptor, preventing APOE4 interaction and inhibiting Aβ deposition. Accordingly, we genetically engineered Lactobacillus plantarum L168 to biosynthesize theanine and niacin, aiming to develop  therapy for Alzheimer's disease and depressions, respectively. Our aim is to assist patients suffering from depression and Alzheimer's Disease in reclaiming their cognitive functions and emotional well-being.
igem_Sustech-Med_2024: Cyclic-oligonucleotide-based anti-phage signaling system (CBASS) is a type of anti-phage defense system that is homologous to the animal cGAS-STING innate immune pathway. The CBASS system consists of two parts: oligonucleotide cyclase and effector. During phage infection, oligonucleotide cyclase produces signal cyclic oligonucleotides, and the effector is activated by the cyclic oligonucleotide, which causes cell death through membrane damage, DNA degradation, and other means. We use a variety of methods such as the type IV secretion system to introduce the CBASS system into the Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm through plasmid transformation, and use virulent phages for infection to achieve the purpose of treating Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The project verified for the first time that the CBASS system can assist phages in the treatment of biofilms, and its significance lies in providing the world with strategies for biofilm-related infectious diseases.
igem_DNHS-SanDiego-CA_2024: Currently, advancements in synthetic biology are often limited by the lack of biosensors. Recently, a paper presented a library of ~2000 E. coli promoters fused to GFP. The goal of this project was to test 10 different molecules with each promoter as a starting point for biosensor development. First, we screened each molecule-promoter pair to identify which ones produced the highest fluorescence. Then, the top few promoters for each molecule were titrated under increasing concentrations of their respective molecule. Due to inconsistencies in the data, we created fresh strains, made uncontaminated media, corrected mislabeled promoters, and regrew promoters with low cell growth. A Deep Learning model was created to predict whether any promoter-molecule pair would produce significant fluorescence in the initial screen. Prominent strains were also analyzed with molecular docking and used to create theoretical parts for future experimentation. In general, this research makes important contributions to biosensor development.
igem_ECIB-PKU_2024: Black fungi which appeared in the wastewater from Chernobyl suggests that melanin may possess radioprotective properties within microbial organisms. In daily lives, radiation comes from sources such as ultraviolet rays, electronic products, medical radiation procedures, and even nuclear wastewater. Furthermore, radiation in space exploration is undoubtedly set to become a key topic of focus in the future. To search for methods of radiation protection, we are planning to employ the tools of synthetic biology to identify effective strategies for radiation defense. We have constructed different strains of microbial organisms to find best solution to produce melanin and have tested their ability of radiation resistance. Also, we are working on hydrogel material which supports microalgal-bacterial co-culture. Our goal is to offer new perspectives and solutions to tackle the challenges of radiation. We firmly believe that through persistent endeavors, we can ensure the safety and success of humanity’s journey through the cosmos.
igem_Tsinghua-M_2024: We use adenosine deaminase acting on RNA(ADAR) to construct a RNA sensor in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, trying to build a toolbox to better understand and utilize the information provided by RNA. This sensor is expected to sense any RNA signal we want and express any selected gene. By confocol microscopy, flow cytometry and other experiments, We successfully proved the activity of our sensor, which can be well expressed in yeast and show high signal intensity. We further apply RNAssay into multiple applications: in situ detection of multigene expression; engineering strain security system; in vivo monitoring of splice variants. Our result shows that RNAssay holds the potential to be a powerful tool for in vivo RNA sensing,  easy to operate, and widely applicable.
igem_BKEA_2024: Kidney stones affect over 10% of people, with pain often compared to childbirth. The problem with current treatments is their invasive and sometimes painful nature and their cost, making them inaccessible to many. Worse, 50-80% of sufferers experience recurrent stones. To avoid people having to endure having kidney stones multiple times. We propose using GMO Lactic acid bacteria, engineered to express oxalate oxidase. The bacteria will be administered through yogurt since it is a widely consumed beverage in arid parts of the world where low water quality and high temperatures lead to increased kidney stone formation. To prove the concepts behind our idea, we successfully transformed our bacteria and proved the enzymes ability to break down oxalate. Furthermore we designed four new programmes to ease the process of conducting docking simulations for future iGEM’ers.
igem_Vilnius-Lithuania_2024: Our global consumption of adhesives will reach 24.7 million tons, but most are made from toxic, non-biodegradable chemicals. Synhesion offers a solution with natural, biodegradable adhesives. We develop a recombinant manufacturing system in E. coli for the efficient and tunable production of the strongest naturally found glue - holdfast. Our system is multiple-fold faster, more controllable, and predictable than the natural one. It uses cost-effective, widely accessible, and renewable feedstocks - glucose, while the strongest available chemical glue, epoxy resin, requires expensive oil-based chemical precursors. Additionally, we developed a new E. coli strain by eliminating competing pathways, enhancing adhesive yield. Our proteins have potential in the medical field and targeted drug delivery systems. We also developed educational tools for diverse audiences. We partnered with Universities of Third Age, launched the “MinkMitą” podcast, a mobile game “Bacteriomania”, organized the "SynFolk" event cycle, and created a children's book to inspire scientific curiosity.
igem_Bielefeld-CeBiTec_2024: Cystic Fibrosis (CF) is the most prevalent inherited disorder, characterized by mutations in the Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator (CFTR). In human lungs, dysfunctional CFTR leads to a decrease in mucociliary clearance, ultimately resulting in organ failure and death. Current treatment strategies are limited in terms of speed, precision, and effectiveness, often failing to achieve long-lasting improvements. Additionally, high costs and limited accessibility of pharmaceuticals contribute to a poor prognosis for many patients worldwide. PreCyse offers the next generation of prime editing technology (PrimeGuide) and our optimized lipid nanoparticle (AirBuddy) for the lung-specific delivery of therapeutic mRNA. We introduce our highly sensitive and context specific reporter system to measure Prime Editing Efficiency. We improved our technology in organoids from human nasal epithelial cells of CF patients, targeting the most common genetic alteration (F508del). Our efforts contribute to a future where cost-efficient, easy-to-use, and accessible therapeutics counteract promote personalized medicine.
igem_SZPU-China_2024: In the wake of the outbreak, people have become more concerned about how diseases are transmitted and have developed good mask habits. However, it is worth noting that some pathogenic bacteria can be transmitted through the respiratory tract for infection and other routes such as the digestive tract. In this project, we pay special attention to the transmission of pathogenic bacteria at the excretory opening, and based on Escherichia coli Nissle 1917, we strengthened its defense and attack system through synthetic biology methods, and developed a product that can effectively occupy the ecological niche and continuously inhibit pathogenic bacteria.
igem_HBUT-China_2024: SUPERB, by using machine learning , predicts potential efficient mutant types and the glycosylation mutation sites from the known PET hydrolase database to enhance the efficiency of plastic degradation in mild and acid conditions. Furthermore, molecular docking is performed with the mutated enzyme and PET, HEMT to identify the most optimal mutant variant. At the same time, by optimizing the chassis cell Pichia pastoris and expression elements, a strain with high expression of plastic degrading enzyme was constructed. Combined with the way of biological transformation, the plastic degradation products of terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG) are synthesized into bacterial cellulose to realize the recycling and upcycling of plastics.
igem_UZurich_2024: Global food systems are increasingly pressured by climate change, unsustainable agricultural practices and social pressures, such as political instability and population growth. Key challenges including environmental instability and desertification threaten food security. RhyzUp presents a sustainable solution by enhancing biofilm production in rhizobacteria to improve plant resilience under stress conditions like drought. Our project makes use of the symbiotic relationship between plants and rhizobacteria to optimize biofilm formation only when in proximity to plant roots, which improves water retention, nutrient uptake, and protection against environmental stressors. By genetically modifying Pseudomonas sp. IsoF, we aim to increase the production of cyclic di-GMP (c-di-GMP), a second messenger involved in the formation of biofilms. This is done by upregulating diguanylate cyclases (DGCs) to increase c-di-GMP production and inhibiting a phosphodiesterase (PDE) to prevent its degradation. Our goal is to create a sustainable approach by leveraging synthetic biology to enhance agricultural resilience.
igem_Bangkok-NMH_2024: Breast cancer remains a primary global health concern. Dendritic Cell (DC) vaccines are a promising immunotherapy that targets tumors using neoantigens. However, personalizing these vaccines requires mRNA sequencing, which is likely unavailable. ASPINE aims to address this issue by developing a machine-learning model to predict neoantigen expression using DNA sequences. We conducted four experiments using the Xpresso model, the first two using an obtained genome sequence and the latter two using an acquired patient data. The second and the fourth experiments have a shorter input sequence length to control for our shorter WES data in experiment four. With acquired patient data, the third experiment yielded an R-squared of 0.329 (RMSE: 0.440). The fourth experiment had an R-squared of 0.294 (RMSE: 0.443), showing improved performance compared to non-patient data. Future work will focus on optimizing the model and refining transcription start site classification to improve prediction accuracy.
igem_EPFL_2024: Post-war landmines and unexploded ordinances (UXOs) can cause injuries or death, pollute land and restrict economic activity long after conflicts have ended. Synplode aims to address this problem. We have engineered bacteria designed to detect and break down TNT and RDX, the two most common explosives found in degrading landmines and UXOs. Our solution is designed to achieve three tasks: first, it detects the explosives and signals their presence; second, it breaks down these explosives into non-explosive derivatives; and third, it confirms the UXO is safe. To deploy this system safely and efficiently, we have built an aerial bio-drone capable of dispersing our bacterial solution over contaminated areas. This provides a scalable, cost-effective, and risk-free method for clearing UXOs. We believe that our approach has the potential to revolutionize the demining process, offering hope to communities still living under the threat of landmines and UXOs.
igem_SDU-Denmark_2024: We aim to develop a minimally invasive, non-hormonal treatment for endometriosis by using a plasmid to induce apoptosis in endometriotic tissue while sparing healthy endometrial cells. Studies show that estrogen receptor β (ERβ) is upregulated >100-fold in endometriotic cells, while estrogen receptor α (ERα) is downregulated. Both are regulated by estrogen. We aim to create conditions where increased ERβ and decreased ERα expression activate the ERβ promoter, leading to BAX gene transcription from the plasmid. BAX is a protein involved in apoptosis, and its increased expression should induce cell death in endometriotic cells. In healthy cells, where ERα is upregulated and ERβ is downregulated, BCL2 gene transcription is promoted by the ERα promoter, helping protect healthy cells from apoptosis. This approach aims for selective treatment of endometriotic tissue without harming normal cells.
igem_Boston-BOSLab_2024: The reliance on porcine-derived heparin poses significant risks, including contamination, supply chain volatility, and ethical concerns. Our team engineered a novel, scalable bacterial system using E. coli Nissle 1917 to biosynthesize heparin. By introducing key enzymes involved in the heparin biosynthesis pathway, we enable E. coli to produce heparin from its naturally occurring precursor, Heparosan. This personalized approach eliminates contamination risks from similar polysaccharides while ensuring a reliable supply of high-purity heparin. Our design not only addresses the ethical and religious concerns surrounding porcine products but also offers a sustainable alternative for global heparin production.
igem_XJTLU-CHINA_2024: DHA is a crucial omega-3 fatty acid vital for brain and retina health, especially for cognitive function and fetal development. It exists in various forms, including natural triglycerides, ethyl and monoglycerides, and phosphatidylcholine, each differing in bioavailability. Phospholipid forms are generally considered more efficiently absorbed. XJTLU-CHINA's current focus is on biosynthetic phospholipids, particularly DHA lysophospholipids, to innovate industrial production methods. By improving the synthesis and availability of these forms, the team aims to enhance DHA's health benefits, contributing to advancements in biotechnology and its application in human health.
igem_XJTLU-Software_2024: iGEM parts registry is an open database containing DNA elements after years of uploading and contribution by iGEM teams. However, the internal data quality is uneven, and some parts have low integrity and only contain sequences without description, optimization, and contribution. In addition, within the iGEM parts registry, the presentation of the result includes text and pictures that lack clear index and quick screening. Therefore, we design an AI Agent, 'Chatparts', that integrates iGEM parts information utilizing RAG (Retrieve-Augmented Generation) system to re-organize the information management and retrieval of parts. After the implementation of RAG, fine-tuning is another essential part of our model training, intending to make the model perform better in particular domains. We also developed a community called iGEM ChatParts Community to establish a platform for the usage of our AI Agent and the communication of iGEMers.
igem_Bolivia_2024: Bolivia is facing a severe mercury contamination crisis, largely due to artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM), which poses significant threats to local ecosystems and human health. Conventional mercury detection methods are costly and complex, limiting their accessibility for affected communities. To address this challenge, iGEM Bolivia proposes a bacterial biosensor capable of detecting mercury contamination. This innovative technology enables real-time monitoring and provides a portable, sensitive solution for detecting organic mercury—the most toxic form to living organisms. By empowering Amazonian communities, protecting biodiversity, and enhancing public health, the biosensor directly aligns with several Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), and SDG 15 (Life on Land).
igem_ULC_2024: Currently, around 2 percent of deaths are caused by tuberculosis, especially those possessing drug resistance. Efficient identification of drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis is urgently required for a fast and scientific treatment. The prevalent polymerase chain reaction (PCR), the chief method used in drug-resistance testing, relies on high-cost equipment and lacks sample point-of-care testing (POCT). Along the research work of Deng Academician's group, our team utilized the sulfur binding domain (SBD) technique to develop a new POCT tool. This protein category embeds sulfur into its hydrophobic cavity and recognizes phosphorothioate DNA(PT-DNA) by hydrogen bonds and electrostatic interactions between the SBD and the DNA. Our project aspires to test SBD's binding capacity to select target-oriented proteins. In the future, these proteins will act as the main ingredient for one detection kit for drug-resistant tuberculosis and contribute to better and timely treatment for patients.
igem_THISDL-United_2024: Our project developed a biocontainment system integrating a temperature-based mobility arresting and logic gate-based killing “double-safe” system, eventually achieving goal of minimizing environmental risks due to the unintentional leakage and consequences of engineered chassis organisms from the lab. The logic gate based killing system coupled the temperature-sensitive regulatory system PR-cI857 regulatory system with a genetic circuit employing toxin-antitoxin systems, to ensure that the engineered cyanobacteria are not able to survive in non-permissive conditions, such as natural environments with night temperature typically below 30°C, but grow normally under laboratory conditions (37°C). The mobility arresting system is constructed based on the crRNA (CRISPR-dCas12a) targeting cell pili.  Our temperature sensing system avoids the addition of any exogenous chemical inducer, not only cutting down the cost but also decease any secondary chemical contamination. Our system could also be implemented in many other bacterial chasses readily with minor modification.
igem_ABOA_2024: To make long space exploration missions possible, we cannot rely on continuous shipments from Earth and life support systems need to be regenerative. Currently, oxygen and water are recovered and regenerated on the ISS but long missions call for closing the carbon cycle as well.  Growing plants for this purpose requires large amounts of resources in the space setting. At the same time, cellular agriculture is emerging as a promising new technology for producing food on Earth with low land use and resource requirements. Could we utilize this technology in space? This is the question we set out to solve.  In our project AstroVita, we mapped out potential opportunities and challenges in utilizing cellular agriculture in space, developed a synthetic biology solution to improve the vitamin content of microbial food and modeled a microbial system for use in space.
igem_HiZJU-China_2024: Rare earth elements include scandium, yttrium, and fifteen lanthanide elements, which are valuable natural resources. The scarcity and importance of rare earth elements draw our attention to how to sustainably mine, recycle, and utilize them. This year, the HiZU-China team from Zhejiang University is committed to developing sustainable biomining technology for rare earth elements, achieving efficient recovery through the integration of bioleaching, biosorption, and biosafety modules. Ultimately, we are dedicated to building a future of clean production and sustainable utilization of rare earth elements, allowing them to better serve the development of human society.
igem_NUDT-CHINA_2024: In light of an increasingly aging population, numerous of individuals are experiencing insomnia symptoms precipitated by endocrine imbalances. Intensifying pressures and escalating workloads are also disrupting adults’ natural sleep patterns. Insomnia caused by circadian rhythm disorders have emerged as a significant health conundrum. Melatonin is widely recognized as the first-line treatment for insomnia, but excessive consumption can lead to adverse effects like headache and dizziness. Notably, MTNR1A receptors paly a more directly role in regulating circadian rhythms, whereas MTNR1B participate in various physiological activities. A drug specifically targeting the MTNR1A is needed to treat insomnia caused by circadian rhythm disorders. Inspired by synthetic biology principles, an innovative small molecule drug screening platform has been developed. This platform introduces a novel exogenous melatonin signaling pathway, enabling the screening potential MTNR1A agonists and natural essential oils that activate melatonin receptors. Our project provides a robust foundation for developing therapeutic agents targeting insomnia.
igem_XJU-China_2024: Bioenzymatic degradation of polyethylene is expected to become a new means of harmless plastic treatment in the future because it is able to convert plastic wastes into carbon dioxide, monomers, and value-added compounds, which is more environmentally friendly and in line with the sustainable development strategy than some chemical recycling strategies that require high temperature and high pressure as well as a large amount of toxic reagents. In this experiment, the polyethylene degradation effect of polyethylene-degrading enzymes produced by 16 laccase sequences, 2 hydrolase sequences and 5 alkane monooxygenase sequences was finally verified by using synthetic biology and bioinformatics methods. It provides new insights into the mechanism of polyethylene pollutant degradation by bioenzymes from XJU-China.
igem_TokyoTech_2024: Pesticides play a crucial role in modern food production. However, current chemical pesticides face various challenges, including environmental changes due to climate change, the issue of resistant species, and their impact on the environment. RNA pesticides, which use the principle of RNA interference, are gaining attention as a means to address these problems associated with chemical pesticides. However, their low durability in natural environments poses a barrier to practical application. MOVE is a module that encapsulates RNA within membrane vesicles, which are surface-presented by functional proteins. Through MOVE, the effective duration of RNA pesticides is extended, maximizing the impact of the RNA. We are pioneering the future of agriculture by doing the following: MOVE RNA pesticides, MOVE pest control, MOVE agriculture.
igem_SYPHU-China_2024: Seborrheic dermatitis (SD) is a chronic, recurrent skin disease influenced by factors such as genetics, immune status, and skin microbiota. Our project introduces a novel treatment using engineered Lactobacillus reuteri expressing the MFP5 adhesive protein from mussels, enhancing adhesion to the skin. This modified L. reuteri promotes antimicrobial peptide (AMP) expression to target and kill Malassezia, a key contributor to SD. Using deep learning, we design AMPs and optimize the promoter and operon to sense extracellular fatty acid concentrations, enabling precise gene expression. Once Malassezia's substrate is depleted, it dies, achieving biological control of SD.
igem_HKPOLYU_2024: Pancreatic cancer has the lowest survival rate among common cancers, with a five-year survival rate below 7%. In addition to curative surgery, chemotherapy such as gemcitabine is applied to patients at advanced stages. The poor prognosis of this disease can be attributed to the lack of targeted therapies and emergence of chemotherapy resistance. Our project aims to address these treatment challenges by using an innovative approach to generate dual-targeting nanobody called Panobody which targets EGFR and c-MET simultaneously, to inhibit pancreatic cancer cell growth, and to overcome gemcitabine resistance. Our pilot data not only improved therapeutic efficacy but also significantly reduced production costs and time, thus enhancing accessibility. Through various outreach activities and stakeholder consultations, we have systematically engaged the broader community to inform our research, ensuring that our proposed solution is not only scientifically rigorous, but also promises substantial social and economic benefits.
igem_East-Coast-Biocrew_2024: More than 70% of the world’s cocoa production originates from Cote d'Ivoire and Ghana. The process involves clearing out large sections of African rainforest for cocoa plantations. Furthermore, cocoa farming generally involves child and slave labor. To combat this, we are creating a synthetically produced chocolate flavoring that will eliminate the need for natural cocoa farming. We chose four of the most prominent flavors in chocolate (theobromine, pyrazine, furaneol and phenylethylamine) and worked to produce them in Lactococcus bacteria. To do this, we started by cloning the genes onto a plasmid, inserting them into the Lactococcus, inducing gene expression with the compound nisin. To evaluate our results, we will use GC-MS to measure the levels of each compound present in our bacteria. Furthermore, we interviewed and incorporated feedback from various experts and nonprofits into our project, which allowed us to have a more comprehensive understanding of stakeholder needs and perspectives.
igem_FHS-NB-ZJ-China_2024: The implementation of precision medicine in cancer requires precision diagnosis and precision therapy. Given the severity of peach gummosis as a disease of peach trees, coupled with its association with age, and taking into account our school's proximity to the prestigious World's First Peach Garden, we have taken a pioneering approach by considering peach trees as our cancer patients and implementing precision medicine strategies. For this year's competition, we studied the literature and carried out field research to gather as much information as possible. We have completed the hardware part of a simple fluorometer that can be used to diagnose gummosis disease in peach trees. However, we still need to learn as much related knowledge and bioinformatics skills as possible to search for treatment targets, and we need to collect more data to complete the software part of our simple fluorometer.
igem_Hopkins_2024: With over 90% of cosmetic surgeries requiring the use of plastic-based meshes for soft tissue support and securing implants, the risk of introducing microplastics and their subsequent adverse health effects runs high. It is clear that there is a need for a bio-based alternative. We propose a silk-based mesh, dubbed Caddisgraft, to solve this issue. Caddisfly silk is a wet adhesive secreted by aquatic caddisfly larvae to protect against the elements, and thus boasts a high tensile strength, biodegradability and non-cytotoxic properties. Our team hopes to develop a yeast strain capable of expressing caddisfly silk for purification and mass production into Caddisgraft surgical meshes. This yeast strain would be created through a novel synthesis method that stitches together highly repetitive silk protein motifs until the desired number of repeats is reached. Ultimately, Caddisgraft hopes to reduce post-operative pain and encourage better tissue regrowth in cosmetic surgery patients.
igem_UCAS-China_2024: Programmable Logic Devices (PLDs) have become pivotal in the development of digital circuits. Unlike traditional digital chips, which have fixed internal circuits that cannot be modified post-production, PLDs allow for manual reconfiguration after manufacturing, enabling them to perform various logic functions. A primary objective of synthetic biology is the application of electronic engineering principles to cellular and biomolecular systems. By manipulating different genetic circuit modules, cells can be engineered to perform specific tasks akin to digital devices. Integrating PLDs into cellular systems opens the possibility of programming cells to exhibit reliable, robust, and diverse behaviors. Existing powerful tools in biology, such as recombinases—a robust recombination framework—and CRISPR interference (CRISPRi), an effective NOT gate widely used in gene circuit design, facilitate this endeavor. This project aims to utilize recombinase and CRISPRi to construct programmable logic pathways in organisms, thereby enabling the systematic programming of cellular behaviors.
igem_Warwick_2024: Less than 10% of rare earth metals are recycled from electronic waste. We present an engineered strain of Methylobacterium extorquens that is able to enrich lanthanides from a homogenous mixture. M. extorquens was engineered to display chemotaxis towards the affordable amino acid aspartate. This biological system facilitates the movement of lanthanides towards an aspartate plug. Lanthanide uptake was optimised via the expression of the protein LanM, which reduces the cellular stress caused by lanthanides. Genetic engineering parameters were informed by mathematical and computational models, including a gene regulatory network model; agent-based and PDE models were also employed to evaluate the experimental setup.  This concept can be implemented industrially to enrich lanthanides from electronic waste for recycling. Additionally, the principles can be applied to other biologically rare elements in the same waste mixture to enrich multiple metals simultaneously.
igem_HKUST-GZ_2024: Coral bleaching, exacerbated by rising sea temperatures and intense light exposure, threatens the survival of coral reefs worldwide. Existing solutions often lack scalability or interfere with coral physiology. We, offers an innovative synthetic biology approach to enhance coral resilience. We engineer the symbiotic bacteria Endozoicomonas to express a light-shielding chromoprotein in response to environmental stressors. This protein reduces excessive light reaching zooxanthellae, the photosynthetic algae within corals, thereby mitigating oxidative damage without disrupting essential cellular functions. By incorporating a regulated genetic circuit sensitive to heat and light, we ensure the chromoprotein is produced only under stress conditions, preserving normal coral and bacterial activity otherwise. This strategy mimics the natural protective effects observed in turbid waters, where reduced light intensity lessens bleaching events. Our solution aims for sustainable, long-term integration into coral ecosystems, offering a scalable method to combat coral bleaching induced by both high temperatures and intense light.
igem_HS-Alpha_2024: There are over 300 million cases of General Anxiety Disorder (GAD) worldwide, causing stress and physical symptoms like pain and insomnia. Aromatherapy, particularly with Sandalwood album oil (SAO), can help relieve these issues. However, SAO is scarce and expensive due to low yields and the endangered status of its source plant. We aim to address this by engineering E. Coli and C.Serevisiae to produce SAO’s key chemicals, creating a sustainable and accessible alternative to traditional methods that take 25-30 years. This project could make SAO’s therapeutic benefits more widely available.
igem_HS-Beta_2024: The increasing prevalence of plastic pollution, particularly marine litter, poses a significant environmental challenge. As highlighted, an estimated 5.25 trillion plastic particles, weighing over 268,000 tons, are estimated to be present in the world's oceans. Microplastics, which are particularly problematic due to their small size and difficulty to degrade, can induce a range of toxic effects, including oxidative stress and metabolic disorders in marine organisms. The innovative approach of employing genetically engineered E. coli BL21 (DE3) expressing surface-displayed PETase and TfCa encapsulated within the BASH device represents a promising strategy to tackle the growing issue of microplastic pollution in marine environments. By combining advanced genetic engineering techniques with a robust encapsulation system, this project has the potential to enable practical and sustainable solutions for plastic waste degradation. The proposed framework aims to provide an effective biological method for degrading harmful microplastics.
igem_AFMU-China_2024: We have chosen food-grade Lactobacillus NZ9000 as the chassis cells and designed two protein expression systems:  (1)Foodborne-stress induced expression system for FGF21(fibroblast growth factor 21) -LMWP (low-molecular-weight protamine). As the concentration of cholate in the intestine increases after meals, the GroESL promoter initiates transcription and promotes the secretion of fusion proteins by the engineered bacteria. The LMWP facilitates the entry of FGF21 into the bloodstream, and FGF21 improves tissue insulin resistance.  (2)Constitutive expression system that displays Akkermansia muciniphila P9 protein on the membrane. P9 protein binds to the ICAM-2 receptor on intestinal epithelial L-cells, releasing GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1), which promotes insulin secretion. We hope that our engineered intestinal Lactobacillus can provide a novel approach for the long-term relief of T2DM by coordinating and leveraging the body's glucose-lowering mechanisms in a non-invasive, long-lasting, and more humane way, thus aiding in the alleviation, control, or even cure of diabetes.
igem_TUM-Straubing_2024: Cell-free transcription and translation (TXTL) is a powerful tool that enables biomolecule production directly from DNA, bypassing the need for living cells. This allows for faster prototyping and production. Our project builds on recent TXTL advancements by using a genetically modified E. coli BL21(DE3) autolysate strain, featuring tardigrade protein genes CAHS 107838, CAHS 106094, and CAHS 94063. These proteins enhance lysate stability at higher temperatures, eliminating the need for costly cryogenic storage. Additionally, we optimized the energy buffer to lower costs, making expensive equipment unnecessary. This opens up TXTL technology to broader use, especially in resource-limited settings. Our improved system is also ideal for educational purposes, as it reduces the financial burden of maintaining specialized lab infrastructure. These advancements make cell-free systems more affordable and accessible, driving further innovation in synthetic biology across academic, industrial, and low-resource environments.
igem_Tec-Chihuahua_2024: Maize, a staple feeding over 3 billion people globally, holds deep cultural, economic, and social significance, especially in Mexico, where it’s intertwined with identity. However, climate change and water scarcity threaten maize, affecting 40% of global crops and endangering food security. To combat this, Zymetec, a biostimulant, enhances maize's stress resistance by boosting the production of osmoprotectants like proline and glycine betaine by activating the metabolic route, improving water use and reducing oxidative stress. Zymetec safeguards maize's nutritional value, ensuring food security, preserving jobs, and supporting cultural traditions, particularly in regions where maize is central to life.
igem_BNUZH-China_2024: The global problem of microplastic pollution has become a significant challenge for marine and coastal ecosystems, with research shows that mangroves not only effectively block plastic debris but also gradually accumulate it in their soil and sediments. Therefore, the microplastic content in mangrove soils is significantly higher than in other coastlines or marine sediments.    To address these issues, we introduce “Mangroves PE&CO2 Hunters”, a project that has engineered two distinct bacterial species to tackle this environmental challenge. The first, P. aeruginosa, has been genetically modified to more effectively break down PE microplastics. Furthermore, we have engineered R. palustris to sequester CO2 produced during the plastic degradation process. Mathematical modeling, machine learning, biokinetic simulations, neural networks, LLM, and RAG are used to explore the project. Besides, we designed iHP tRi-Cycle to better understanding real-world needs thus refine our project.
igem_TJUSLS-China_2024: PET is a widely used plastic. However, its extensive use has also caused severe environmental pollution. In this project, through multiple rounds of engineering cycles, we optimized the promoter, signal peptide, and culture conditions, successfully constructing a highly efficient ICCG expression system. First, we created an ICCG-GFP fusion protein and used fluorescence intensity to characterize ICCG protein expression levels. During promoter optimization, we generated a Mtac promoter library through random mutagenesis and used a CNN-LSTM model to design and optimize the novel DMtac promoter. For the signal peptide, we screened and optimized the nfaA signal peptide and designed MnfaA mutants using a Markov transfer frequency matrix model. By combining high-throughput screening systems with predictive models, we significantly improved the expression efficiency of ICCG, providing valuable components and tools for future synthetic biology research.
igem_uOttawa_2024: Phytogene aims to provide an affordable and sustainable alternative for synthesizing pharmaceutically and commercially relevant peptides through plant-based production (i.e. biopharming). Specifically, this project focuses on the transient heterologous production of GLP-1R agonists in Nicotiana benthamiana. Our platform consists of three key steps: cloning, plant expression, and purification. Cloning involved the design of plasmids for easy gene insertion and integration (1), plant expression was achieved through Agrobacterium-mediated transformation (2), and purification was completed through the harvesting of leaf crude lysates, followed by affinity chromatography (3). Finally, SOLIDWORKS, a computed-aided design tool, was used to design and simulate a scaled version of the agroinfiltration vacuum chamber. Through the use of an integrative design process, and by making improvements based on finite element analysis (FEA) results, Phytogene can prove its commitment to making biopharming more accessible, providing a scalable and cost-effective solution for peptide synthesis in the synthetic biology community worldwide.
igem_NTU-Taiwan_2024: Discover how NTU-Taiwan’s SAC project is revolutionizing the production of spider silk through AI-driven innovation. By creating a carbon-negative, scalable, and customizable biomaterial, we’re addressing critical environmental challenges while meeting the diverse needs of various industries. Join us on our journey to weave a more sustainable future.
igem_GU-Frankfurt_2024: UV radiation is a leading cause of skin cancer, affecting over 1.5 million people annually. While sunscreens protect the skin, UV filters pose environmental dangers, particularly to marine ecosystems, by contributing to coral bleaching. About 14 tons of these filters enter oceans yearly, harming marine species like mussels, fish, and dolphins, and threatening coral reefs, which support vast biodiversity and human livelihoods. Additionally, these chemicals can disrupt human endocrine systems. To address this, SOLAR offers a sustainable solution using mycosporine-like amino acids (MAAs), naturally occurring in marine organisms, as UV-protective agents. Through synthetic biology, we aim to produce MAAs using E. coli, optimizing production and UV absorption ranges via Petri Nets and NRPS bioengineering, respectively. SOLAR aims to create scalable, reef-safe UV filters without compromising environmental or human health.
igem_Tongji-China_2024: After conducting thorough research into the potential health risks and environmental impacts of existing nail polish products, our project has innovatively developed a unique nail polish. By precisely producing enzyme-induced red, yellow, and blue pigments using engineered bacteria, we enable the free expression of vibrant patterns, offering personalized nail art options to users. Furthermore, we have developed a groundbreaking eco-friendly adhesive material, "AMS," which integrates mussel hybrid protein with hydrogel to enhance both adhesion and environmental performance, providing users with a new, aesthetically pleasing, and healthy nail polish experience.
igem_Thessaly_2024: Olive trees hold deep cultural and economic importance in Greece, accounting for 79% of the country's tree crops. In our region, Thessaly, they are crucial to the stability of farmers' livelihoods. However, olive trees face a significant threat from Verticillium dahliae, a fungal pathogen that causes severe yield losses and tree mortality, especially in the Mediterranean. The lack of effective treatments has resulted in substantial economic losses, posing challenges to farmers' way of life and threatening the environment. With this in mind, our team developed THAELIA, a modular bacterial system that produces dsRNA to precisely target and silence essential fungal genes. By disrupting the growth and virulence of V. dahliae, THAELIA offers a sustainable new approach to fungal control. This approach protects olive trees during critical periods, ensuring the safety of biodiversity, human health, and the environment.
igem_CAU-China_2024: Over a third of the world's population can't afford healthy diets due to poverty, trapped in a dilemma between low income and malnutrition. Nodule Factory produces nutrients with rhizobia, innovatively addressing both issues. Rhizobia are symbiotic bacteria of leguminous plants, and the symbiotic structure of nodules has a naturally microaerobic environment, while DHA and EPA are high-value and microaerobic substances. We deleted specific enzyme genes to increase precursor substances and added regulatory sequences and synthetic gene clusters to enable them to produce DHA and EPA under low-oxygen, high-nitrogen conditions in nodules. Proper inoculation and nitrogen fertilization ensure the efficiency of Nodule Factory, providing impoverished regions with high-added-value legumes for income and nutrition. In the future, we aim to transfer these nutrients to soybeans to further empower the soybeans. Our modular Nodule Factory will pioneer sustainable and microaerobic production, significantly contributing to global sustainability.
igem_BNU-China_2024: Nanodiscs are tiny, disk-shaped structures engineered as drugs, antibodies, or in vitro biological components. Our project introduces a groundbreaking nanodisc-based antiviral therapy, NanoDisguiser, designed to tackle the limitations of traditional methods, such as viral drug resistance.  By using broad-spectrum nanodiscs therapy with virus-specific receptors, these nanodiscs act as decoys, luring and disrupting viruses before they can infect cells. This cutting-edge approach provides a powerful and versatile defense against a wide range of viruses, including new and mutant strains. We're also working to validate and commercialize this technology as an injectable antiviral solution, aiming to redefine antiviral therapy in a post-pandemic world.
igem_USTC_2024: One of the major challenges in the treatment of solid tumors arises from the immunosuppressive nature of the surrounding tumor microenvironment（TME）, which weakens the immune system's cytotoxic ability. Currently, therapeutic strategies targeting the solid tumor microenvironment have gained extensive attention, while most existing treatments still confront with challenges such as off-target risks. Our team has noticed that harmless Escherichia coli Nissle 1917(EcN) can automatically colonize the tumor microenvironment, demonstrating excellent targeting potential. Therefore, we plan to utilize the angiogenesis mechanism driven by vascular endothelial growth factorin （VEGF）in the human body. We plan to genetically modified EcN to express VEGF competitive binding receptors under ideal conditions of TME and conduct a surface display in ECN. By integrating and consuming VEGF in the tumor microenvironment, we plan to reduce its concentration in the TME, thereby effectively inhibiting angiogenesis in tumor areas and ultimately suppress tumor proliferation.
igem_NNU-CHINA_2024: The supply of grain is the foundation of people's livelihood. However, with many agricultural fields in various regions suffering from drought, diseases, pests, and other attacks, many people still live in hunger. Using biopesticide to enhance crops' resistance to abiotic and biotic stresses, while promoting crop yield is an available solution. 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) is a sophisticated and sustainable biopesticide, especially when compared to the various highly toxic and non-degradable chemical pesticides currently in use. The exploration of the biological manufacturing of 5-ALA in recent years has driven our research. However, issues such as the stability of ALAS gene expression, the obsolescence of targets, and the low efficiency of screening for target strains still persist. This project addresses these three issues by utilizing CRISPR-associated transposon system, enzyme-constrained model, and droplet microfluidic high-throughput screening technologies to explore solutions.
igem_JLU-NBBMS_2024: JLU-NBBMS 2024 has developed the BIOTARGET, an advanced biological system iteratively engineered using bacteria. This system integrates modular design concepts from synthetic biology, RNAi technology, attenuated Salmonella, and nanotechnology to precisely target and treat chemotherapy-resistant cancer cells. It enhances tumor recognition with a targeting module, suppresses chemoresistance gene expression with a gene regulation module, ensures Salmonella's controllable behavior within the body through a safety module, and facilitates precise drug delivery via a nanoparticle-mediated module. We have further validated the metabolism, dynamics, and efficacy of the BIOTARGET using mathematical models and cell experiments to ensure its safety and efficacy, aiming to provide personalized treatment options for patients and enhance the effectiveness of chemotherapy drugs.
igem_USTC-Software_2024: We are attempting to build a highly interactive and comprehensive bioinformatics service platform. The platform includes a fully optimized single-cell analysis pipeline that can be applied to synthetic biology research requiring transcriptomics analysis. In addition, we have explored the current applications of deep learning models, and have also integrated a community within the platform to allow users to communicate and discuss with each other at any time.
igem_MSP-Maastricht_2024: MSP-Maastricht is addressing coastal eutrophication, a local and global issue. Excessive fertiliser run-off from agriculture, a key economic sector of the Netherlands’ economy, has polluted waterways, spreading into marine ecosystems. This leads to ocean acidification, anoxia, and harmful algal blooms, which intensify climate change and disrupt biodiversity. Natronaut focuses on engineering the marine bacterium Vibrio natriegens to mitigate nitrate pollution in coastal waters. By harnessing its rapid growth and metabolic capacity, we aim to assimilate excess nitrates and convert them into single-cell proteins (SCPs), which can serve as sustainable livestock feed. This innovation reduces the need for conventional feed crops and fertilisers, promoting resource efficiency and circularity. Our project addresses the environmental challenge of eutrophication by not only reducing eutrophication but also working to prevent its recurrence. Ultimately, we aim to convert agricultural waste into valuable biomass, turning the tide on nitrate pollution.
igem_SZ-SHD_2024: Mars is a potential destination for human migration. However, future explorers will face significant challenges, including the lack of natural food resources and oxygen, toxic and poor soil for crop production, and limited synbio toolkit. We proposed solutions across four key areas inspired by a series of human practices. First, to provide sustainable nutrition, we aim to co-culture engineered yeast and cyanobacteria to produce essential compounds such as lycopene, nerol, and limonene. Second, to convert Martian soil into arable land, we isolated nitrogen-fixing bacteria and used directed evolution to enhance bacteria’s resistance to Martian toxins.  Third, we introduced updates to our TTTT system, released in 2023, which now reduces plant transformation time by up to 50%, encouraging more iGEM participants to engage in plant synthetic biology. Finally, as a creative endeavor, we applied DNA data storage to archive significant records of Earth's biodiversity and culture for future generations
igem_thessaloniki_2024: Multiple Sclerosis is an increasingly prominent, multifactorial disease that affects almost 3 million people worldwide,with that number being expected to increase exponentially. Its treatment is currently centered around symptom management and decelerating its progression, as there is no available cure. Recognising this major gap in modern therapeutics, we developed NeuroMuSceteer; a modular, precision medicine, holistic therapy. It involves T- cells that are engineered to selectively target specific disease antibodies and act as immune regulators (Tregs),boosting the immune system and the CNS. Furthermore, we included two molecular structures, one that detects and one that releases microRNA agents in target cells, repairing nerve damage. The design was made in collaboration with various stakeholders in both research and healthcare, with the purpose of tackling all aspects of Multiple Sclerosis with accuracy and safety. Its modularity also allows it to be adapted for various autoimmune disorders, making it a useful tool for future researchers.
igem_UPF-Barcelona_2024: The SkinBait project aims to develop an innovative approach to treat skin diseases caused by external organisms, with a current focus on scabies, a condition caused by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei. It involves engineering the skin bacterium Cutibacterium acnes to produce toxins that are lethal to scabies but harmless to humans. Our project had two main parts: the expression of Cry proteins and the expression of endolysin regulated by an RNA thermometer. We optimized gene circuits for Cry toxin production using C. acnes and E. coli, developed safety mechanisms using RNA thermometers and the endolysin, and designed experiments to evaluate Cry toxin efficacy and biocontainment strategies. Several mathematical models were included that simulate what effect our approach would have. Through this design, we aim to create a safe, effective, and biologically contained treatment for skin parasites, setting the foundation for broader applications in skin disease treatment.
igem_AshesiGhana_2024: Coastal erosion and plastic pollution are growing threats to coastlines worldwide, and Ghana is no exception. These environmental challenges have severely impacted communities near the coast, destroying homes and infrastructure, displacing families, and burdening the economy heavily. Despite efforts to address these issues, current solutions have proven ineffective in providing lasting relief.  The Sea Titans aim to deliver a groundbreaking and sustainable solution to combat plastic pollution and coastal erosion. Our innovative approach involves the Pentacone, a structure equipped with advanced biotechnology designed to decompose PET plastic in the sea and reduce coastal erosion. This Pentapod is designed to self-regenerate when damaged, ensuring longevity. This circular approach not only cleans our seas but also strengthens coastal defenses.  As Sea Titans, we want to create a future where our oceans and coastlines are cleaner, more resilient, safer for coastal communities and contribute to the global fight against pollution and environmental degradation.
igem_NEFU-China_2024: This project focuses on the reutilization of food waste by employing directed evolution of key enzymes to improve the production of 7-methylxanthine (7-MX), a high-value compound, with caffeine from coffee grounds as the substrate. This research not only provides an innovative and sustainable solution for the reutilization of coffee grounds, thus promoting the sustainable development of the circular economy, but also opens up new possibilities in the biosynthesis of methylxanthine compounds.
igem_OUC-Haide_2024: Livestock farming has long been essential for providing high-quality protein and other animal by-products. Antibiotics are extensively used in this industry to ensure stable production. However, misuse of antibiotics leads to environmental residues and the emergence of antibiotic-resistant superbugs, posing significant human health risks. β-glucans, naturally occurring β-D-glucose polysaccharides found in grains, bacteria, and fungi, offer a potential alternative to antibiotics due to their immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory. β-glucans, particularly from Aureobasidium melanogenum BZ-11, can be efficiently produced via fermentation. This fungus isolated from mangroves secretes extracellular polysaccharides, including β-glucans, but also melanin and pullulan, which complicate the purification process. Using synthetic biology techniques, we employed Cre-loxP to block the secretion of melanin and pullulan, enhancing the purity of β-glucans. Additionally, introducing an oxygen uptake system improved yield. Our optimized fermentation process allows for the efficient production of β-glucans, presenting a viable antibiotic alternative for livestock feed, potentially mitigating antibiotic misuse.
igem_Grand-Tokyo_2024: Thrombosis accounts for one in four deaths worldwide. "Thrombosis" is a general term for diseases caused by blood clots obstructing blood vessels, including myocardial infarction, stroke, pulmonary embolism, and cardioembolic stroke. This is a significant issue in Japan, which is experiencing an aging society. Among the G7 countries, Japan has the highest percentage of elderly people within its total population. However, current treatments for Thrombosis consist of side effects that heavily affect the body. which is why we decided to use nattokinase, which is found in the Japanese traditional food, “Natto”. Nattokinase demonstrates strong thrombolytic activity by enhancing the effects of the fibrinolytic enzyme plasmin present in the body, therefore easy to consume the body, less resistant from consumers, and is a new preventative solution for Thrombosis. Our product form of tea is easily consumed daily and without health issues as barriers.
igem_Barcelona-UB_2024: Reneurish aims to genetically modify neural progenitor cells (NPC) to overexpress BDNF –a potent neurotrophic factor- to tackle the challenges attributed to neural transplants; low neuronal integration and cell survival.   This overexpression is achieved through the infection of NPCs with an AAV vector. Donor’s NPCs are kept in a reservoir and infected after stroke takes place, then transplanted into the patient’s damaged brain region to enhance regeneration, improving integration, synapsis and minimizing tissue death.  During our investigation, the need for precise monitoring led to the development of a customizable reporter transfection cassette, which can be easily removed during the humanization of the vector.  This study concluded that BDNF can be overexpressed in human NPCs for over 50 days. We observed that an increase in BDNF levels correlates with a higher neural activity, better axon connectivity and higher cell count, without generating aberrant networks.
igem_Hannover_2024: We developed a cellular sensor using genetically modified HEK cells to detect both heavy metals and antibiotic residues. The Hydro Guardian integrates the eukaryotic metal-binding transcription factor 1 (MTF1) pathway for heavy metals and the PASTA domain from prokaryotes, which is sensitive to beta-lactam antibiotics. The sensor was optimized through a sophisticated spectroscopic analysis pipeline and refined using a detailed differential equation-based model, enabling the determination of minimal residue detection limits. Throughout the design process, we collaborated with stakeholders from various fields and contributed over 20 new parts to the iGEM Registry. To validate the sensor concept, we successfully demonstrated the expression of distinct fluorophores, activated by specific promoter-regulator pathways for the MTF1 and PASTA domains, confirming the functionality of the system in detecting target contaminants.
igem_ZJU-China_2024: ZJU-China has designed a new and interesting microbial staining method. On the basis of synthesizing Violacein's highly efficient metabolic modification and addressable RNA scaffold, it uses light-induced DNA recombinase and light-sensitive transcription factors to realize memory pattern drawing, hoping to bring the color of synthetic biology to the fashion industry. Please join us to find fashion!
igem_Peking_2024: Aimed at creating a new methodology for disease diagnosis, GPA combines AI with protease-based circuits to accomplish modularization, the core value of synthetic biology, which is embodied in the design of our system－the variable biomarker recognition part and the constant signal amplification and output part. For the first part, featuring on flexible structures, aptamers (i.e., single stranded nucleotides) recognize variable biomarkers. Additionally, an AI tool－MAGA, has laid foundations for applying aptamers to biomarker binding. With MAGA, given a biomarker of a specific disease, we can obtain different aptamers recognizing it with high affinities. For the second part comes the protease-based circuits to transform and amplify signals. For the third part, a special designed gold colloidal test serves as the output. With GPA, we envision a future where the primary disease diagnosis takes fewer time, costs lower, prioritizes user-friendliness and ensures everyone a healthier life.
igem_NJTech-China_2024: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic intestinal inflammation of unknown etiology and incurable nature. This project utilizes  Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 as the chassis cell, employing six functional modules to address IBD. The sensing module, regulated by the SoxR/SoxS promoter, detects excessive NO, ensuring that the gene circuit is activated only in the IBD environment, thereby enhancing safety and specificity. The therapeutic modules include the immune module (PD-L1), adhesion module (Mfp), and antioxidant module (SOD), which are designed to suppress immune responses, repair damaged intestinal tissues, and eliminate reactive oxygen species, respectively. The lysis module automatically lyses probiotic cells upon their accumulation at the inflammation site, releasing therapeutic proteins. The safety module activates the expression of the MazF toxin via a blue light-responsive promoter, ensuring the engineered bacteria die upon excretion, thus mitigating potential risks.
igem_CUG-China_2024: Given the global increasing demand for mineral resources and the ore grades decline, there is an increasing utilization of microorganisms in biomining to extract valuable metals from low-grade ores and electronic waste. Biomining offers a sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional mineral processing technologies. However, it faces challenges like long leaching cycles, low extraction efficiency, and unspecific bioleaching. The genetic engineering of microorganisms can enhance their capabilities for improved biomining performance promisingly. Acidithiobacillus, a genus of extremophilic acidophiles commonly inhabiting mining process waters and acid mine drainage, is a promising chassis for metal recovery and bioremediation of metal-contaminated sites. In 2024, CUG-China aims to enhance biomining efficiency for nonferrous metals by genetically engineering Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans. This engineered strain incorporates a cyclic di-GMP synthesis module for the enhancement of bacteria-ore interactions, a gold-specific detection module for targeted recovery, and an electron transfer module for further improving biomining processes.
igem_Alma_2024: White-Nose Syndrome affects five of the nine bat species located in Michigan: the Little Brown bat, the Big Brown Bat, the Tricolored bat, the Indiana bat, and the Northern Long-Eared bat. The disease is caused by the fungus Pseudogymnoascus destructans, which infects bats during their hibernation period, causing the collagen in their noses to slowly degrade due to proteolytic enzymes produced by the fungus. This causes the bats to become active from hibernation prematurely, which results in lethargy due to the limited resources. Without the necessary means to sustain life available in the winter season, death is often a result. There is currently no widespread treatment to prevent P. destructans infections in bats. We aim to engineer E. coli that secrete a serine protease inhibitor(s) to prevent collagen degradation.
igem_MichiganState_2024: Many researchers have challenged the degradability of the biopolymer Polylactic Acid (PLA), hugely popular in 3D printing. To address PLA's environmental persistence, we are working to engineer the bacterium Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 to degrade PLA and generate power from its breakdown. S. oneidensis is a gram-negative, facultative anaerobe capable of extracellular electron transfer, and can break down organic material and generate electricity in microbial fuel cells. It utilizes lactic acid as its carbon source to produce electricity. Therefore, we engineered S. oneidensis with genes encoding for PLA depolymerases from 4 bacterial strains. When expressing these genes, we expect that S. oneidensis will be capable of depolymerizing PLA to lactic acid, then using the lactic acid as a substrate for electricity production. The S. oneidensis strains that were successful in degrading PLA will be used in a microbial fuel cell for electricity production with PLA as the carbon source.
igem_BUCT_2024: Cancer is a major health issue, and chemotherapy, while a primary treatment, often has severe side effects and limited effectiveness. Sulforaphane, an isothiocyanate found in cruciferous vegetables like broccoli seeds, has strong anti-cancer properties with minimal side effects. However, its production from plants leads to land waste, high costs, and unsustainable practices. We aim to synthesize sulforaphane de novo in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and use computational and synthetic biology to enhance its yield. This approach will reduce costs, land waste, and deforestation, offering a sustainable alternative that supports global climate change efforts and improves human health.
igem_BJWZ-3-China_2024: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a highly toxic and carcinogenic foodborne pollutant, which seriously threatens food safety and public health. In order to degrade AFB1 that may be generated during the transportation, storage and processing of food, feed and so on in real time, we take Lactobacillus rhamnosus as the chassis, and let the nano-fluorescence system that can specifically bind to AFB1 and the light-induced VVD photosensitive system work together to activate the expression of laccase (CodAGold) that degrades AFB1, so as to achieve real-time degradation of AFB1. In addition, MazF is under the control of a glucose sensitive promoter, to prevent the escape of engineered bacteria and ensure biosafety. This method is expected to provide a valuable strategy for agriculture, animal husbandry and food safety to realize real-time harmless treatment of AFB1.
