Currently, agriculture consumes 92% of the world's water, jeopardizing food systems due to rising competition. Wastewater reuse becomes critical, but 80% is not properly treated, and 11% of crops, especially in the Global South, rely on it. In Mexico, only 5.4% of wastewater is reused, with limited research on emerging contaminants. To tackle this issue, we present Aquasens, a portable system that efficiently detects water contaminants using FRET technology. It features a biosensor that identifies changes in fluorescence when contaminants are detected in a sample. In this project, we present lab results using a FRET system to detect rifampicin, cadmium, and ibuprofen, along with a new version of the device from the previous team. We also conducted social activities to raise awareness about Jalisco's water situation and developed a business plan for future commercialization.
igem_PLKLFC_2024: Prostate cancer is often diagnosed only after symptoms appear, and existing screening methods tend to be either costly or unreliable. Our goal is to develop a new, affordable, and user-friendly screening technique that also targets and eliminates prostate cancer cells. We use PSMA as a biomarker to detect these cells, and a plasmid that triggers the release of Gaussia Luciferase (GluC) in the patient's urine. Additionally, the plasmid promotes the release of an apoptosis regulator (Bax) to help kill the cancer cells. Another important aspect of our project is education. We have created a lesson plan aimed at sparking junior secondary students’ interest in synthetic biology and encouraging their future involvement in the field. Teaching these students in September also provides us with valuable insights from them.
igem_MacquarieUni_2024: Vanillin is an aromatic aldehyde used in food, beverage and cosmetics applications. Worldwide consumption exceeds 16,000 tons annually, with 0.25% from natural extraction from vanilla orchid pods, and the remainder from organic chemical synthesis. The biotechnological production of vanillin offers a promising alternative. In this project, we design and test four different biosynthesis gene clusters to manufacture vanillin from tyrosine in bacteria, using a cumate-inducible control system and a low-copy number broad-host-range plasmid; preliminary LC-MS data indicate that we were successful in making small amounts of vanillin, and that the caffeate-> ferulate reaction (COMT) was rate-limiting in our system. Further evidence for functional expression of the HpaBC monooxygenase was seen from production of a brown melanin-type dye as a side-reaction; we believe this indicates that HpaBC is acting on tyrosine (to make L-DOPA, which polymerises) in addition to the intended reaction on 4-coumarate to make caffeate.
igem_OKstate_2024: This year, the OKstate iGEM team created Healios, a novel treatment designed for the targeted destruction of multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens, such as Staphylococcus aureus. Healios uses an engineered M13 phage to target specific bacteria. The non-infective phage can be conjugated with Rose-Bengal, a photosensitizing dye, which, when activated by a free-moving LED lamp, produces reactive oxygen species (ROS) to kill the bacteria. Due to time limitations, we were unable to complete the pilot system, but we have clearly documented all our designs on the wiki. Throughout the year, the OKState team actively engaged with scientific experts and received valuable advice on project design and how Healios can extend beyond the bench. Importantly, the impact and potential of synthetic biology in public health were demonstrated by engaging K-12 students in the local community. We are OKState Healios!
igem_Jilin-China_2024: Inspired by bioluminescent bay, Jilin-China developed a novel mechanoluminescent hydrogel biosensor. Using luciferase-producing bacteria in sodium alginate hydrogels, the material converts pressure into light. This is a novel approach to translating pressure into light, with applications ranging from eco-friendly touchscreens to cost-effective heart rate monitors, and beyond. We believe it will advance technology and illuminate everyone's future.
igem_WHHS-China_2024: This project aims to create genetically engineered E. coli strains for efficient and comprehensive glyphosate degradation.  The system integrates three key modules: a glyphosate transport mechanism using the phnE1 and phnE2 genes to facilitate rapid uptake, a degradation pathway via phnJ for C-P bond cleavage that converts glyphosate into non-toxic phosphate and glycine, and an AMPA detoxification system employing the phnO gene to further degrade the harmful byproduct aminomethylphosphonic acid (AMPA).  Together, these modules ensure efficient glyphosate absorption, degradation, and detoxification.  Experimental data confirm the strain’s ability to significantly reduce glyphosate and AMPA levels, providing an environmentally friendly solution for herbicide contamination in agricultural settings.
igem_WHHS-Pro-China_2024: This study focuses on developing an engineered phosphate recovery system using two bacterial strains. The first system, PhosLock 1.0, utilizes ice nucleation protein (INP) to anchor phosphate-binding proteins (PBP) on the cell surface, allowing efficient phosphate adsorption. The second system, PhosRegen 2.0, optimizes PBP secretion using the PelB signal peptide, which guides PBP into the extracellular medium. Both systems were experimentally validated for phosphate adsorption and desorption under varying pH and temperature conditions. PhosLock 1.0 demonstrated efficient phosphate binding, but faced challenges with bacterial stability. PhosRegen 2.0 addressed these limitations by coupling PBP with NHS-activated beads, improving both adsorption and desorption efficiency. This dual approach offers a promising solution for wastewater phosphate recovery and lays the foundation for scalable, sustainable environmental remediation technologies.
igem_Tec-Monterrey_2024: The contamination of aquatic environments with 17α-ethinylestradiol (EE2) presents serious ecological and public health concerns due to its endocrine-disrupting effects. To address this issue, we have engineered a novel transcriptional regulatory protein, the Estrogen-Sensitive Transcriptional Element Regulator (ESTER), designed to selectively activate gene expression in the presence of EE2. Several computational tools, including AlphaFold 3, Rosetta, and Chimera, were employed to design this EE2-sensitive protein.
igem_USP-EEL-Brazil_2024: In recent years, cannabidiol (CBD) has gained significant recognition in the medical field as a key component as an adjuvant in treatments for various conditions, including psychotherapeutic therapies. However, in Brazil, the cultivation and commercialization of Cannabis sativa, the plant source of CBD, face strict legal restrictions. This project proposes an alternative method to produce CBD using synthetic biology, bypassing the need for the plant. The plan involves synthesizing cannabidiol through recombinant gene technology in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast), which will express cannabidiolic acid (CBDA), a precursor of CBD. The process utilizes two metabolic pathways: the geranyl diphosphate (GPP) pathway and the olivetolic acid pathway. These precursors are combined in enzymatic reactions to form cannabigerolic acid, which is then converted into CBDA. The CBDA can be purified and transformed into CBD, offering a more efficient production method without the legal complications of Cannabis cultivation.
igem_SZSAIS-Shenzhen_2024: The global issue of obesity continues to rise, affecting numerous countries. In China, for instance, more than 20% of adults are overweight. Obesity contributes to various health problems, including hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and diabetes, posing significant risks to human health. One of the leading causes of obesity is excessive sugar consumption, yet many struggle to reduce their sugar intake. To address this, our team has proposed a practical solution aimed at lowering calorie consumption. This year, we have developed a synthesis method for producing low-calorie sugars by converting widely available glucose into tagatose, a healthier alternative. Through this approach, we hope to combat the obesity epidemic globally.
igem_Squirrel-Beijing-II_2024: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a serious health concern, especially for people who enjoy hot pot. In our previous study, by analyzing blood samples and sophageal cancer tissue from clinical ESCC patients, we screened out sensitive proteins related with fatty acid metabolism, which were necessary in repairing esophageal epithelial cells injury, the level of functional protein played key roles in inhibiting inflammation and malignant lesions in esophageal tissues. Thus, in our present project, we firstly designed exogenous plasmid and constructed a high-level expression system in Escherichia coli, to express high-level of functional protein. Then the protein nanoparticles were prepared with oleanolic acid. Through constructing esophageal epithelial cells injury model, the relieving effects of MFG-E8 protein was evaluated in vitro. By this method, MFG-E8 protein is eventually integrated into containing tablets, which effectively alleviates esophageal epithelial cells damages caused by hot and spicy stimuli, and reduces the incidence of ESCC.
igem_Squirrel-Beijing_2024: Due to increased pressures, staying up late and insomnia have become common across all age groups. This chronic circadian rhythms disruptions are proven to accelerate pathological progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). What can we do in suppressing the adverse progression? In our previous study, by using an AD mouse model with artificially disrupted circadian rhythms, we proved that rose flavonoids had significant inhibitory effects on the adverse progression. Thus, in the present project, we create "ROSE” plan to develop functional tea drinks and alleviates circadian rhythms disruption injuries, including: Firstly, Recreate an cellular AD model with Aβ42 protein; secondely, Observe and identify specific genes by transcriptomics; thirdly, Supplement rose flavonoids into cells and measure expression levels of protein and signal pathway; lastly, Evaluate the inhibitory effects on AD progression and prepare functional tea. Our team innovatively provides dietary intake regulations in reducing AD risk of circadian rhythms disrupted people.
igem_GEC-Beijing_2024: Denim jeans, a timeless fashion staple, often require treatments like bleaching, fraying, and stain removal. Traditional methods, such as chemical bleaching and mechanical fraying, pose environmental and health risks, including water pollution and excessive resource use. To address this, our iGEM team, “New Jeans,” developed an enzyme-based solution using engineered E. coli  BL21. We produce laccase for bleaching, cellulase for fraying, lipase for stain removal, and catalase to boost laccase efficiency. This eco-friendly "Jeans Care Kit" reduces chemical reliance, cuts water usage, and allows consumers to customize denim care at home. Our approach promotes sustainability by extending denim's lifespan and reducing waste, with cost-effective large-scale enzyme production.
igem_Squirrel-Shenzhen_2024: Copper ion contamination is an increasing threat in China, affecting food safety and agriculture. In response, we developed a dual-plasmid biosensor using synthetic biology to detect copper ions. Our system employs the E. coli endogenous copper sensor CueR to regulate a signal plasmid. Upon binding with copper, CueR activates the pCopA promoter, expressing a fluorescent protein, mVenus, in proportion to copper concentration. Additionally, we fine-tuned the system using a promoter library for CueR overexpression. This portable, low-cost biosensor offers a reliable solution for monitoring copper pollution, ensuring safer food and water for consumers.
igem_LCG-Global_2024: Our team initially addressed the challenges of chronic disease management, focusing on hypertension, hyperlipidemia, hyperglycemia, and obesity. We developed a home-based Point-of-Care Testing (POCT) system for detecting key biomarkers like glucose and uric acid using plasmid-based biosensors engineered with synthetic biology. These biosensors offer enhanced accuracy and reduced recalibration compared to traditional electrochemical methods. To complement the biosensors, we designed a hardware platform that seamlessly integrates with biomarker detection. Human practices shaped the system’s key performance specifications, such as affordability, compactness, and biosafety. As the project evolved, we incorporated modularity, allowing for multi-biomarker detection and scalability. This flexible, open-source platform enables easy biomarker replacement and broader health applications, contributing to future innovations in personalized diagnostics and for the iGEM community..
igem_LCG-China_2024: LCG-China 2024 enhanced the 2014 Imperial College bacterial cellulose modification system by resolving legacy issues and developing a modular decoupling platform to improve protein-cellulose interactions. Our system incorporates a bacterial cellulose scaffold (curlisfiber-spytag) with fusion proteins (spycatcher-fusion protein of interest), allowing for efficient binding of proteins that typically do not bind with cellulose. This modular design supports future upgrades of individual components, increasing the system's versatility for various applications. Utilizing this platform, we developed a biodegradable adhesive bandage functionalized with antimicrobial peptides, addressing limitations of traditional wound care products. Additionally, to ensure safe AI use in synthetic biology, we established an AI safety policy guideline and a proposal specifically for the iGEM community, providing a robust framework to mitigate risks in AI-driven bioengineering projects.
igem_Oxford_2024: The rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents a critical global challenge, demanding innovative approaches to combat resistant bacterial strains. With the deluge of new AMR bacteria and the slowdown in antibiotic discovery, the human and economic cost of AMR is increasing at a worrying pace. Our project addresses this by leveraging the RP4 conjugation system to selectively transfer the engineered OneRing plasmid into target bacteria. This modular plasmid encodes CRISPR-Cas12a and a guide RNA array, enabling targeted bacterial killing through precise DNA cleavage. This precision ensures a targeted approach to bacterial killing without harming surrounding bacteria in the microbiome. By modifying the guide RNA array, OneRing can be adapted to tackle various types of bacteria. This versatility allows for a range of applications across human health and livestock farming. Our design's modularity also enables future expansion to address diverse bacterial challenges in other fields.
igem_UMA-MALAGA_2024: Aflatoxin B1 is a potent mycotoxin produced by Aspergillus fungi, which is commonly found in cereals and feeds, posing significant risks to public health and the food industry. Its persistence through high temperatures and food processing makes it challenging to eliminate. Chronic exposure to AFB1, even in small amounts, can accumulate in the body and increase the risk of liver cancer and other diseases by damaging DNA through its reactive metabolite, AFB1-exo 8,9-epoxide (AFBO). The AflaxOFF project addresses this issue by engineering Saccharomyces cerevisiae to act as a biosensor, providing early detection of AFB1 contamination in food, as well as a probiotic, preventing AFB1 absorption in the intestines, thereby protecting both humans and animals from the toxin. AflaxOFF actively engages with stakeholders, including farmers and food industry professionals, to ensure that the technology meets real-world needs and fosters community awareness about AFB1 risks.
igem_VIT-V_2024: The project tackles the public health challenge posed by high UV Index levels in Vellore, Tamil Nadu, which contribute to around 300,000 annual cases of non-melanoma skin cancer. While traditional sunscreens effectively block UV radiation, they often contain harmful chemicals that can disrupt hormones and damage the environment. This project proposes engineering Escherichia coli to overexpress genes in the Xanthophyll pathway, enabling the production of carotenoids like zeaxanthin and violaxanthin. These natural pigments offer antioxidant properties and can be integrated into skincare products for broad-spectrum UV protection. By employing recombinant DNA technology, this project aims to provide eco-friendly alternatives to chemical synthesis, addressing both skin health and environmental sustainability. The incorporation of these carotenoids into cosmetics aligns with the rising demand for safe, plant-based beauty solutions, ultimately contributing to a healthier market in India while mitigating skin cancer risks associated with UV exposure.
igem_RDFZ-CHINA_2024: Our project addresses the critical issue of petroleum pollution by developing an innovative bioremediation system. We engineered E. coli and B. subtilis to degrade residual oil using enzymes like AlkM and laccase, while also enhancing efficiency with surfactants. Additionally, we integrated plant-microbe cooperation by utilizing E. coli to produce the plant hormone IAA, promoting phytoremediation. To ensure biosafety, we incorporated a suicide system to prevent gene leakage. This multi-faceted approach offers a sustainable and scalable solution for addressing petroleum contamination.
igem_UFlorida_2024: To further the global understanding of sepsis, our team developed in silico and in vitro bone marrow organoid models. In silico, we were able to successfully simulate the growth and differentiation of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) into a healthy steady-state iPSC-derived bone marrow organoid. We also implemented a pathogenic function into the model and achieved states of aseptic death and full recovery to an altered equilibrium. This model predicted and quantified the immune system's cellular and inflammatory response to a sepsis-like infection. Additionally, we improved the biomanufacturing of in vitro iPSC-derived bone marrow organoids by optimizing iPSC culture and organoid production techniques. We established an improved four-phase differentiation protocol that enhanced aggregation, oxygen level tolerance, organoid viability, and morphology. The development of these dual ex vivo platforms provides deeper understanding of the cellular changes triggered by sepsis in human bone marrow.
igem_NENU-China_2024: Beer, a popular alcoholic beverage, uses grains like barley, oats, and wheat, which can be affected by Fusarium head blight (FHB) in warm, humid conditions. FHB, also known as scab, produces mycotoxin DON, posing a threat to human health and economies. It is urged to seek control methods to eliminate DON pollution in foods and feeds.  We engineered a new yeast with extrachromosomal plasmids to separately enhance the cell wall adsorption and the DON enzymatic degradation efficiency in Saccharomyces pastorianus. To analyze the molecular mechanism of yeast DON adsorption and discover gene loci related to yeast's ability to adsorb DON, we constructed a model to predict the DON adsorption ability of different yeasts.
igem_Patras-Med_2024: The Lethe project proposes a new therapeutic approach in gene therapy for the treatment and management of Alzheimer's Disease. By targeting the dephosphorylation of tau proteins, we increase the chances halting the disease and reversing the underlying neurodegenerative course. Our goal is to enhance the activity of the phosphatase PP2A, which is related to the process of tau dephosphorylation. This up-regulation will be facilitated indirectly by microRNA-195, a molecule associated with various pathological processes of the disease. We will introduce microRNA-195 into nerve cells using rAAV-carrying exosomes, modified with the RVG29 peptide that binds specifically to target nerve cells. These modified exosomes will interact with the surface of the target cells and release rAAVs expressing microRNA-195, inhibiting the processes responsible for the disease's pathogenesis.
igem_Harvard_2024: Adaptive Cell-Free Quorum Integrated Release Engine (ACQuIRE) is a modular platform designed to improve safety and scalability in synthetic biology, particularly for bioremediation and biomanufacturing. ACQuIRE encapsulates engineered Escherichia coli within biocompatible PEG-Ficoll protocells, enabling controlled protein production and quorum sensing-triggered lysis at a defined population density. This system enhances biosafety by retaining genetic material within the protocell, reducing the risk of horizontal gene transfer. ACQuIRE offers a reliable alternative to traditional kill switches, utilizing a density-dependent lysis mechanism to minimize the risk of mutations and uncontrolled proliferation. The platform's use of minimal media reduces autofluorescence and side reactions, improving experimental clarity and reproducibility. ACQuIRE provides a scalable, standardized method for safe and controlled production of genetically modified organisms, addressing critical challenges in synthetic biology.
igem_WUXI-DSAS_2024: Corn sheath blight caused by Rhizoctonia solani is one of the most destructive fungal diseases, causing serious losses to corn grain production. Although traditional chemical fungicides can effectively resist sheath blight, they also bring a series of environmental and other problems. Spraying double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) to induce gene silencing (SIGS) is a potential new tool for sustainable and environmentally friendly plant disease control. This project designed a sequence that can target and silence pathogenicity-related genes, RsCAT (R. solani catalase), constructed it into an expression vector, and used E. coli HT115(DE3) to produce dsRNA. Experiments have shown that after spraying RsCAT-dsRNA, the transcription level of the RsCAT gene was downregulated, and corn showed obvious disease resistance. In summary, Our project not only provides a novel strategy for the management of corn sheath blight but also carries significant potential for broad-spectrum application in the control of a variety of crop diseases.
igem_DUT_2024: Our team has created a modular, tunable mRNA platform tool that empowers the platform with cell-selective and protein-regulatory functionality.
igem_UCopenhagen_2024: The breastmilk meant to nurture new life could be exposing infants to invisible dangers - But what if we could change that? Breastmilk can be contaminated with endocrine disrupting contaminants (EDCs) like BPA, PCBs, and dioxins. These harmful compounds can accumulate in breastmilk and pose a risk to infants. Without proper disposal, these toxins can cause long-term health issues. Inspired by the liver, we present SUPERMOM, a yeast-based contaminant-induced system that detects and detoxifies harmful EDCs in breastmilk. SUPERMOM uses biosensors and phase I and phase II liver detoxifying enzymes to keep breastmilk safe for infants. We envision SUPERMOM to be integrated into everyday breastfeeding products, such as milk bottles or nipple shields, through a dual-layer encapsulation system. This system ensures that while breastmilk interacts with SUPERMOM, the yeast remains securely contained, offering parents a safe and effective way to detect and detoxify contaminated breastmilk.
igem_CSW-UD_2024: As global temperatures increase, human populations rise, and food insecurity worsens, there is a need for immediate action to sustain humanity. Scientists aim  to increase crop yield to battle the current circumstances, focusing on improving RuBisCO, a key enzyme in photosynthesis. However, they often overlook RuBisCO’s chaperone RuBisCo activase (RCA) which creates thermal limitations. The activase regulates the activity of RuBisCO by removing inhibitory sugar phosphates, RuBP, from RuBisCO's active sites to maintain RuBisCO’s catalytically active form. While RuBisCO is thermostable at temperatures above the optimal carbon dioxide assimilation rate, RCA is highly heat-sensitive, so our project aims to enhance RCA's heat resistance. To detect the heat-sensitive regions of RCA, we used machine learning (MutCompute) and implemented point mutations in those regions. Though we were unable to use our assays due to time constraints, our research serves as a strong foundation for further study on this topic.
igem_Mexico_2024: This project aims to develop an environmentally friendly pesticide that poses less risk to human health compared to existing products in Cosalá, Sinaloa, Mexico. We will use Saccharomyces cerevisiae for the production of piperamides, bioactive compounds derived from black pepper (Piper nigrum). These piperamides have been proven effective against the larvae and eggs of the fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda), the most significant pest of maize in Mexico and globally. We have integrated insights from climate experts, politicians, farmers, and other stakeholders to shift our perspective towards considering sustainable alternatives. We don't just embrace our solution; we embrace solving the problem. Our diverse models provide strong evidence that bioinformatics and mathematics are powerful tools for developing impactful solutions, from differential expression analysis to molecular dynamics simulations and ODEs simulations.
igem_JIASHU-China_2024: Our project, "Coli Bond," explores an innovative approach to information security by leveraging genetically engineered E. coli bacteria. We developed a method to encode data within DNA sequences, disguising the information as natural protein sequences to evade detection. To enhance security, we designed a multi-layered system that ensures bacterial strains only grow under specific conditions and includes a self-destruction mechanism triggered by elevated temperatures. This prevents unauthorized access and maintains data integrity. Additionally, our project addresses the challenges of encoding complex logographic languages like Chinese by integrating unique input methods. Our work demonstrates a promising application of synthetic biology in the field of information security, combining advanced genetic engineering with practical data protection strategies.
igem_JIASHU-Shanghai_2024: The program aims to address skin aging in menopausal women due to a decline in estrogen. For menopausal women, estrogen is especially important in skin care, and common beauty and skin care products on the market do not solve this problem. Our team selected E. coli Nissle 1917 as the chassis microorganism and constructed three systems, including genistein production system, bacterial cellulose production system, and light-controlled induced suicide system. Genistein can supplement estrogen, bacterial cellulose is used for hydration, and the light-controlled suicide induced suicide system ensures biosecurity. Through special production and use methods, the products provide a safe and efficient skin care experience for middle-aged and elderly women.We are also actively promoting STEM education for women, helping them to achieve holistic growth from the inside out.
igem_JIASHU-SouthChina_2024: The JIASHU-SouthChina team is developing an innovative solution for stress relief and depression management through the Joy-filled Drink project. By engineering E. coli Nissle 1917, we have successfully produced kaempferol and GABA, two compounds known for their positive effects on mood and mental health. To optimize kaempferol production, we explored the use of fusion enzymes and tested various linkers (GGGS, GGGS2, TPTP, TPTP2), identifying those that significantly improved the kaempfero yield. Additionally, we examined the impact of multi-copy genes and found that F3H boosts production while FLS has the opposite effect. Our vision is to integrate these compounds into fruit tea, bringing an accessible and natural option for emotional well-being to the market. This project showcases the power of synthetic biology in addressing mental health challenges.
igem_Tuebingen_2024: We are developing modular bacterial regulators by integrating structural Biochemistry with bioinformatics approaches based upon structure predictions, molecular dynamics aswell as evolutionary information based analyses such as shannon entropy and direct coupling analysis. Bacterial LuxR family regulators have been proven to be modular, with a typical domain architecture consisting of a signal reciever domain in the form of for example a two component system signal reciever or small molecule binding domain, aswell as a LuxR family DNA binding domain. Multiple Studies did show that it is possible to swap DNA binding domains of these regulatory proteins under specific circumstances, achieving an altered DNA binding specificity, and therefore an altered regulatory output for any given signal. Our Plan is to develop and apply metrics to guide the design of such "rewired" bacterial regulators.
igem_UESTC-China_2024: The UESTC-China research team has successfully developed an innovative colorimetric biosensor utilizing microplastic anchoring peptides, thereby providing a rapid and user-friendly method for the detection of microplastics. Furthermore, by employing advanced synthetic biology techniques, the research team implemented a streamlined "one-pot" process that integrates a surface display system with a multi-enzyme system to convert PET plastic waste into high-value vanillin, thus fostering environmental sustainability. Through the integration of cutting-edge technologies, including machine learning and directed evolution, the project significantly improved the detection accuracy of the anchoring peptides as well as the efficiency of PET plastic degradation processes. Ultimately, this project realized an integrated solution that encompasses both detection and degradation, complemented by real-time data visualization, thereby offering a comprehensive and sustainable framework for the reutilization of plastic waste.
igem_RainsACA-China_2024: In order to achieve the goal of using cucumber epidermal hairs to synthesize flavonoids, the problem that this project needs to solve is: Is it possible to modify the key gene CsTBH and flavonoid metabolism gene (PAL) of cucumber epidermal trichome. By using synthetic biology and analyzing the difference in product content, it is possible to determine the effect of the CsTBH-CsPAL system on the synthesis of flavonoids and produce more flavonoids in cucumbers.
igem_IOANNINA_2024: West Nile Virus (WNV) is a neuroinvasive pathogen responsible for severe encephalitis,with no specific antiviral treatment currently available. In this study, we propose an innovative antiviral strategy utilizing the RNA-targeting Cas13d system to combat WNV-induced encephalitis. Our approach involves designing guide RNAs (gRNAs) through a custom algorithm, tailored to efficiently target WNV RNA sequences. To enhance the safety and specificity of the Cas13d system, we integrate a regulatory mechanism involving a synthetic NFAT (nuclear factor of activated T-cells). This engineered NFAT ensures that Cas13d expression is induced only upon viral infection, levaraging the calcium influx triggered by WNV entry, which activates endogenous NFAT signaling. By linking the antiviral response to WNV-specific cellular changes, this system minimizes off-target effects and reduces the risk of unintended immune activation. This regulated antiviral platform holds potential as a novel therapeutic approach for treating WNV-induced neurological disroders.
igem_SMU_2024: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths globally, and China has a high incidence of liver cancer. In 2020, new cases and deaths from liver cancer in China accounted for approximately half of the global total. Traditional treatment methods such as surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy have limited effectiveness in advanced HCC. Despite significant breakthroughs in T cell immunotherapy in the treatment of hematologic malignancies, the tumor immunosuppressive microenvironment is a unique feature of solid tumors, and a key factor in inducing tumor immune escape, setting them apart from hematologic malignancies. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are the primary organizers of the immunosuppressive microenvironment and promote HCC immune escape through various mechanisms. In this project, a dual-specific engineered T cell named “Bispecific T-cell Leaper” has been developed to target HCC and CAFs, aiming to disrupt the immunosuppressive microenvironment and reverse HCC immune escape.
igem_TERMOSZ-Selye-HUN_2024: Histamine is one of the key factors of starting an inflammation process. Limiting the level of histamine effect can be an appropriate approach in those cases, where you can anticipate the histamine level increase. On our skin this includes some chronic diseases such as psoriasis, but more often would be useful in handling the acute increase of histamine level, such as a wasp bite. Aspiring the decrease in oral histamine administration may also help to prevent some acute GI inflammation and smoothing the symptoms of some chronic bowel diseases. Our group main aim is to create a complex synthetic biology solution attacking the biologically functional histamine. The solutions we plan to use, are using DAO and HNMT enzymes and ssDNA aptamers known from the scientific literature.
igem_IIT-ROORKEE_2024: Our project focuses on the development of a groundbreaking diagnostic method for early Red Rot detection, utilizing smartphone iSPR to quantify DNA-Protein interaction signals. This innovative approach offers a cost-effective means of identifying ITS rDNA Biomarkers from C. falcatum fungus, addressing the critical need for early diagnosis of a fatal disease, called “Cancer of Sugarcane”, Red-Rot. By harnessing the unique binding properties of ZAP1 protein with our specific rDNA sequence, we aim to create a highly specific and sensitive diagnostic tool that can detect Red-Rot’s related DNA in soil or stalk sample. This project seeks to revolutionize Red-Rot detection by providing a convenient, accessible, and accurate point-of-care solution, with the potential to transform farmers life decreasing the probability of spread of the disease and the loss caused by it.
igem_WegoTaipei_2024: Blood transfusion mismatches, particularly involving the Rhesus D (RhD) blood type system, can cause severe hemolytic reactions, posing significant medical risks. The availability of RhD-negative (RhD-) blood is limited in many regions, creating challenges for emergency and routine transfusions. This study aims to develop universal red blood cells by preventing the recognition of Rh antigens by anti-D antibodies. Using bioengineering techniques, we designed smaller, more efficient forms of anti-D antibodies, such as single-chain variable fragments (scFv) and single-domain antibodies (sdAb). Additionally, we developed a conversion kit to streamline the blocking of Rh antigens. Experimental methods included plasmid digestion with XhoI and NdeI enzymes, ligation into the pET-28a vector, and transformation into competent Escherichia coli B cells for protein expression. This approach aims to create a universal blood supply, mitigating transfusion complications associated with Rh incompatibility.
igem_SRE-China_2024: WGX-50, a previously reported drug candidate for Alzheimer's disease, is derived from Zanthoxylum bungeanum Maxim. Since that time, its pharmacological actions for the long-run benefit of human health had been extensively investigated. However, in terms of its anti-aging effect, there are very limited studies for reference. In this work, WGX-50 was first reported to extend lifespan in C. elegans, and it conduces to heat shock proteins (HSPs) longevity pathway, in which key genes like hsf-1, hsp-16.2, and hsp-90 were transcriptionally upregulated. Importantly, hsp-90 was revealed as a putative target for WGX-50 using molecular dynamics simulations. Four novel hits, namely F44E5.4/.5, sri-40, F59B2.12, K09C6.9 revealed by RNA sequencing, were first tested to be irrelevant to the lifespan extension effect of WGX-50 through RNA interference. Thus, our results offer primary insights on the medicinal application of WGX-50 in long-term and anti-aging healthcare.
igem_jky-wuhan-china_2024: Hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) is a common infectious disease caused by enterovirus, such as EV71,which is common in children. Due to the immature immune system and imperfect hygiene habits of infants and young children, the disease is easy to spread in this vulnerable group and lead to serious consequences. We use a novel programmable nuclease Argonaute and synthetic biology techniques to develop a simple, rapid and accurate assay. The speed and affordability of the method will ensure that all educational institutions and medical institutions can use it, and it will better improve the prevention and control of infectious diseases in epidemic education institutions.
igem_NWU-CHINA-A_2024: Mucopolysaccharidosis type II (MPS II) is a rare X-linked recessive disorder, classified as severe or mild based on central nervous system involvement. Current treatments are limited, costly, and risky for severe MPS II patients. Exosomes, extracellular vesicles (30-150 nm), have shown promise as drug carriers, particularly engineered exosomes, which are used in treating brain diseases and cancers due to their low immunogenicity, targeting, and ability to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). This year, the NWU-CHINA-A team investigated the enzyme-carrying capacity and BBB penetration of engineered exosomes, offering new therapeutic ideas and applications for drug delivery systems.
igem_WLSA-ShanghaiAcademy_2024: Diabetes mellitus is a global health issue. Isoorientin, a plant-derived compound, has shown potential in managing diabetes by promoting insulin secretion and improving insulin sensitivity. However, its low natural concentration limits large-scale production, highlighting the urgent need for alternative biosynthesis methods. To address this challenge, our study focuses on the biosynthesis of isoorientin by engineering E. coli to express the C-glycosyltransferase Gt6CGT.  The Gt6CGT gene was initially cloned into the pET-21a(+) expression vector, and a recombinant plasmid was constructed using seamless cloning technology.  This plasmid was subsequently transformed into E. coli Rosetta (DE3) competent cells, where protein expression was induced by IPTG.  After expression, the enzymatic activity of Gt6CGT was confirmed through microplate reader and HPLC analysis.  This system provides a robust foundation for the efficient biosynthesis of isoorientin and supports its potential large-scale production as a natural therapeutic for diabetes.
igem_Institut-Le-Rosey_2024: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounting for 85% of cases. Current detection methods are either invasive or costly, limiting accessibility. Our project aims to develop an affordable, non-invasive diagnostic kit for early detection of NSCLC by targeting EGFR mutations, a key biomarker. Using padlock probes and rolling circle amplification (RCA) coupled with a split lettuce probe detection mechanism, the kit amplifies and identifies the mutated sequence in cell-free DNA from patient blood samples. This process eliminates the need for expensive PCR equipment, making the test accessible in low-resource settings. The fluorescent signal generated by the lettuce probe binding to the amplified product indicates the presence of the mutation. By providing a preliminary diagnosis, this kit can help identify high-risk individuals earlier, increasing the chances of timely treatment before the cancer advances to critical stages.
igem_Tongji-Software_2024: ATLAS.Y is a specialized tool designed to optimize protein subcellular localization within yeast. It uses signal peptide and linker databases to engineer fusion proteins with precise localization signals. The software employs the ESM-fold model for fast 3D structure prediction, the Rosetta model to assess protein stability, and the CAD-score to ensure functional consistency. DeepLoc 2.0 assists in verifying localization accuracy. Additionally, ATLAS.Y uses a graph-based deep learning algorithm for directed evolution, allowing proteins to adapt to specific microenvironments. For applications requiring precise control, the system offers a dynamic version integrating optogenetics for spatiotemporal regulation of protein localization.
igem_HW-ShanghaiUnited_2024: The area of global desertification is expanding at a rate of 23 football fields per minute, posing a significant threat to the availability of land. Over the years, China has actively fulfilled its commitments under the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification and has made notable progress. However, the global rate of desertification remains alarming, severely threatening ecological security and sustainable development. As a group of high school students committed to a responsible future, we have engineered Komagataeibacter xylinus to produce bacterial cellulose (BC) more efficiently. BC possesses exceptional water-retention properties, is environmentally friendly, and does not hinder the growth and development of tree roots, making it an ideal candidate as a water-retaining matrix material for afforestation in deserts. By enriching BC around the roots of tree, we aim to enhance the drought tolerance and survival rate of newly transplanted trees, thereby contributing to the mitigation of land desertification.
igem_Hangzhou-MedX_2024: In the face of economic pressures and epidemic challenges, China's breastfeeding rate is a concern. The high cost and limited nutritional value of formula milk have placed a financial burden on many families. This project aims to use Saccharomyces cerevisiae for the low-cost production of two important nutrients in the growth of infants and young children: lactoferrin and N-acetylneuraminic acid. We introduced the human lactoferrin synthesis gene and the high-yield Neu5Ac synthesis gene into Saccharomyces cerevisiae cells using the pESC-URA plasmid vector, respectively. Subsequently, the functions of the engineered cells were verified using a variety of methods, including kits and SDS-PAGE, and the production of the target product was finally confirmed. Our goal is to provide economical nutritional supplements that promote the health and well-being of infants and relieve the psychological stress of mothers who are unable to breastfeed themselves.
igem_GSLZ-A_2024: Regarding cancer solutions, remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and enhancing the activation of immune-infiltrating cells through multifaceted strategies is considered one of the most promising avenues to overcome these challenges. Currently, a series of immune checkpoint inhibitors have gained clinical acceptance to improve the immunosuppressive environment within the tumor and enhance the anti-tumor effects of CD8+ T lymphocytes. And synthetic biology serves as a possible approach to enable the coordinated release of defective cytokines in the tumor microenvironment (TME) to be able to produce similar immunomodulatory effects. Targeting the OSCC tumor microenvironment to achieve barrier clearance and immune enhancement through specific components or structures in the TME that induce tumor immunosuppression has aroused our interest. Through studying the literature and communicating with expert predecessors, we focused on choosing the bacterial-encoded hyaluronidase Hy and flagellin FlaB as our key research molecules.
igem_McMasterU_2024: As the climate crisis intensifies and the cost of living rises, the demand for a circular economy has never been greater. Project Chloronova leverages microalgae as a scalable carbon-sequestering organism by partnering with major industrial polluters in our hometown of Hamilton, Ontario to reduce carbon dioxide emissions while producing high-value biomolecules. Unlike bacteria, microalgae offer the unique ability to perform post-translational modifications, make multiple heterologous proteins and withstand antimicrobial mechanisms. Inspired by our human practices research, Chloronova engineers microalgae to produce antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), thus addressing the alarming rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and the urgent need for sustainable bioproduction. Using PEG-mediated transformation in a cell-wall deficient strain of Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (cw15+), we are able to introduce our plasmid into the chloroplast DNA of the microalgae. By optimizing AMP production within C. reinhardtii, we are creating a scalable, modular biofactory. It’s a new day, and algae is here to stay.
igem_KFUPM-Saudi-Arabia_2024: Skin and Soft Tissue Infections (SSTIs) encompass a broad spectrum of infectious conditions that affect the skin and underlying soft tissues. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) accounts for over 50% of SSTI cases. In the United States, SSTIs affect more than 14 million outpatients annually, with 900,000 requiring hospitalizations. The rise of antimicrobial resistance threatens the efficacy of antibiotics used to treat SSTIs, prompting the search for alternatives. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), especially those produced by thermophilic bacteria, have gained attention as potential solutions. In our project, we utilized bioinformatics tools to identify novel AMP genes in the genome of the thermophilic bacteria Brevibacillus borstelensis AK1, a thermophilic bacteria isolated from a hot spring in Saudi Arabia. We then designed a plasmid to contain these AMP genes and cloned them into Escherichia coli for heterologous expression, aiming to develop a novel AMP-based treatment for SSTIs in the face of rising antibiotic resistance.
igem_Ulink-SZ_2024: The accumulation of shrimp and crab carapaces waste poses serious environmental hazards. Despite the potential to convert these chitin-rich materials into high-value chitooligosaccharides (COS), the scarcity and high cost of recycling technologies mean that these carapaces are often overlooked. By selecting from Bacillus species and site-directed mutating, we will obtain high-activity chitin deacetylases (CDA) and chitosanases (CsnB) and improve the enzymatic method to produce COS from chitin, thereby enhancing the recycling and utilization of waste carapaces.
igem_SHSID-China_2024: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) is a group of autoimmune diseases that involves the inflammation of the digestive tract. It is currently becoming much more prevalent in Asia due to rapid urbanization and the adoption of Western dietary habits. IBD has a lower onset age than most other chronic diseases. However, there is no effective treatment for IBD. In this context, we utilized genetic engineering techniques to produce a macromolecular drug, Interleukin-18-binding-protein (IL-18BP) to treat IBD. In our project, human IL-18BPa and IL-18BPc genes were modified with SUMO to improve the protein stability, Fc to achieve potential targeted drug delivery, and His tag for purification. Our research results revealed the protein's ability to successfully lower IFN-gamma levels (a sign of inflammation), demonstrating its anti-inflammatory effect and potential application in IBD treatment.
igem_HWFLA-Beijing_2024: Tumors pose multifaceted harm, including life-threatening risks, organ damage, complications, psychological impact, and reduced quality of life. Genetically engineered bacteria have emerged as a promising strategy for disease diagnosis and treatment. These engineered bacteria have been used to monitor cancer liver metastases, liver dysfunction, and various gastrointestinal disorders, such as inflammation and infection. Certain bacteria, like Salmonella and Escherichia coli Nissle (EcN), can selectively colonize tumors due to their ability to infiltrate the hypoxic cores of immune-deficient tumors. In this study, we utilized a lactic acid-responsive promoter to control the expression of anti-PD-L1 antibody or azurin killer protein. EcN was engineered as a tumor-specific drug delivery system to target tumors and locally release drugs, thereby inhibiting tumor growth and reducing both drug dosage and cost. This approach could provide new insights and strategies for cancer treatment.
igem_UppsalaUniversity_2024: Our project addresses environmental and health concerns associated with synthetic dyes by exploring biological alternatives. We aim to reduce the toxic chemicals used in dye production by focusing on two objectives: the discovery of new biological pigments from environmental microorganisms, and the mutation of new colours in existing chromoproteins for large-scale production. Specifically, we are targeting AmilCP to make new colours more suitable for industrial use. Using size exclusion chromatography, SDS-PAGE semi-native analysis and bioinformatics, we aim to identify novel chromoproteins using AI tools for protein engineering. Synthetic dyes, widely used in textiles and other industries, are major pollutants, especially in water systems. Biological pigments offer a sustainable alternative. Inspired by previous research into microbial pigments, our project aims to contribute to a greener future by providing scalable and environmentally friendly solutions to current dyeing practices.
igem_PINGHE-MCA_2024: Traditional sweeteners have become a research focus due to issues such as high calorie content and high blood sugar levels .D-Psicose,as an emerging low calorie sweetener, combines good sweetness with health benefits such as reducing fat and lowering blood sugar. Due to its scarcity in nature, there are two synthetic methods: chemical synthesis, which pollutes the environment, and biological synthesis, which is highly favored for its environmental friendliness and efficiency. However, the existing enzyme species of the key enzyme in the biosynthesis of D-Psicose, 3-isomerase, have poor thermal stability and low expression.In this study, we selected the coding genes of D-psicose 3-epimerase from different sources, induced the expression and purification of the target protein in Pichia pastoris, and detected its enzymatic properties to screen D-psicose 3-epimerase with good thermal stability.
igem_BZK-SH_2024: As a widely distributed eukaryotic microorganism found in nature, some fungi have posed significant threats to food safety and human health through infections. Current fungal detection methods, like DNA isolation and gram staining microscopy, require specialized equipment, experimental conditions, and high costs. Lacking direct visualization capabilities also limits their broad use in food safety inspection and clinical diagnosis. Moreover, the accuracy of microscopy can be affected by difficulties in differentiating various fungi from background noise. To address these issues, we designed a fungi-detecting probe utilizing carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs) for their special affinity to fungal cell wall polysaccharides and chitin. By combining CBMs with fluorescent proteins, this probe enables rapid, eco-friendly, and visual in situ detection of fungal contamination in samples from different scenarios.
igem_SubCat-Union_2024: Rotaviruses are the most common causative agents of severe gastroenteritis in children under five years of age. Vaccination is the most effective measure to prevent Rotavirus infection. It was previously shown that the outer capsid viral protein (VP4) is an essential target for developing a recombinant rotavirus vaccine as it mediates the attachment and penetration of rotavirus. However, the current live rotavirus vaccines show reduced effectiveness. Here, we focus on crafting a recombinant rotavirus vaccine with improved efficacy and safety. The coexpression of a human collagen type Ⅲ with VP4 in Escherichia coli was employed to generate oligomerization of recombinant rotavirus vaccines. Further, a stable hydroxyproline-free ABC heterotrimeric collagen mimetic system was used to produce a polyvalent rotavirus vaccine. Importantly, these newly designed vaccines utilize non-infectious virus-like particles with enhanced immunogenicity and protection, which could be considered viable candidates for further development to become a parenterally administered rotavirus vaccine.
igem_SubCat-GreatBay_2024: Nowadays, food safety has not been comprehensively guaranteed mainly due to the severe health risks foodborne bacteria bring. However, current bacterial detection methods are time-consuming and less accessible. Our team believes that these limitations can be improved by developing a more efficient and effective product by coupling gold nanoparticles that have useful physical properties, with Phage-derived bacterial-binding protein (PBP). This biosensor rapidly binds to three specific bacteria (Escherichia coli, Salmonella, Staphylococcus aureus) within thirty minutes, analyzes their concentrations via RGB values on a smartphone app, and sterilizes bacteria using near-infrared (NIR). Additionally, it achieves efficient antibacterial effects under 808 nm light irradiation for 10 minutes. This study is significant for the detection and elimination of foodborne pathogens for both synthetic biology development and practical influences in the food industry. Furthermore, we will investigate the target market to ensure a pragmatic and applicable product is available to our potential consumers.
igem_SubCat-HS_2024: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is one of the most common neurodegenerative diseases. Early screening of the disease is a key measure to prevent the occurrence and development of the disease. NF-L is a universal marker of nerve damage and is elevated in a variety of neurodegenerative diseases, including PD. In the early stages of PD, elevated NF-L levels can be detected. Using α-synuclein, Aβ42, and NF-L as biomarkers simultaneously can improve the sensitivity and specificity of PD diagnosis. Each marker provides a different pathological perspective, making the comprehensive analysis more comprehensive. This study intends to obtain PD-specific markers α-syn, Aβ42, and NF-L through genetic engineering, and use ELISA to verify the accuracy of the obtained proteins, which can lay a good foundation for the acquisition of specific antibodies and the construction of early screening kits in the future.
igem_DBHS-CA_2024: Drug addiction is a chronic condition characterized by compulsive drug seeking and use despite negative consequences. Extensive research shows that surges of dopamine during pleasurable activities affect the brain's reward circuits. G9a, an under-researched gene, regulates dopamine production and release, influencing how the brain responds to addictive substances. Elevated levels of EHMT2 (the coding gene for G9a) are observed in addiction, and our research aims to reduce these levels using RNAi technology, specifically small-interfering RNA. Through a three-component system involving the construction of plasmids altered for overproduction of our gene to be expanded in further research on addiction, siRNA technology tests for optimal concentration and conditions, and a concept model of lipid-nanoparticles as a delivery method, we hope to contribute to the possibility of creating an accessible therapeutic to solve this problem.
igem_Stony-Brook_2025: Targeted delivery of therapeutic proteins toward latent HIV-infected cells remains a major challenge in eradicating HIV. Leading therapies block entry via envelope proteins or coreceptors, as well as reverse transcription. We developed a protein-based delivery system using a detoxified single-chain diphtheria toxin (DTA) as a translocation carrier across the cell membrane. This system delivers large protein cargoes, such as Cas13a, into cells in a receptor-dependent manner. A GP120 gene fragment was added to the fusion protein to act as the ligand for CD4+ T-helper cell receptors. These systems remain under development and low expression of Cas13a-DTA in E. coli (10-beta, Rosetta, and W3110 strains) poses challenges in extraction. Our research complements gene editing and external protein therapies to evaluate HIV cleavage in mimic CD4 receptor cells (HEK293). Quantifications of ssRNA cleavage via RT-qPCR will be presented, suggesting how effectively this treatment could extend to pharmaceutical applications.
igem_OUC-Haide_2025: Globally, nearly 588 million people live with diabetes, and up to 25% of them suffer from chronic, non-healing wounds, facing risks of infection, gangrene, and even amputation. Current conventional therapies are ineffective and cumbersome, exacerbating patient suffering, while advanced treatments remain inaccessible due to high costs, limited functionality, or lack of dynamic regulation. To address this, we introduce “Yeast Medics”—an innovative injectable dressing based on engineered Yarrowia lipolytica and L-DOPA-modified thermosensitive chitosan. This system dynamically senses wound status, displays antimicrobial peptides (Pexiganan) on the yeast surface, and programmatically releases both anti-inflammatory (IL-4) and pro-angiogenic (VEGF) factors. It synergistically addresses the three major challenges of infection, inflammation, and regeneration on a single platform, providing diabetic patients with an integrated, self-driven, low-burden healing solution.
igem_CJUH-JLU-China_2025: Adipocytes can be transformed into cancer-associated adipocytes (CAAs) by cytokines from cancer cells. As CAAs demonstrate distinct gene expression pattern, we aimed to engineer adipocytes that could report such pattern. Systematic analysis revealed that the optimal combination to identify CAAs is PLOD2 and LIF, which could be induced by PAI-1 and CXCL8 respectively. We designed a RADAR sensor that targets the transcripts of PLOD2 and LIF simultaneously and delivered this sensor into differentiated adipocytes. These engineered adipocytes responded to the combined stimulation of PAI-1 and CXCL8 only. Most importantly, these engineered adipocytes responded to the treatment of the conditioned medium from breast cancer cells, revealing the potential of these adipocytes to respond to actual cancer microenvironment. We chose Gaussia luciferase (Gluc), an enzyme to generate luminescence, as output reporter. As Gluc could be secreted into urine, it offers a convenient way to report the results of in vivo cancer monitoring.
igem_XJU-China_2025: The SILK project (Stability-Integrated Industrialization Leveraging Key plasmids) addresses the critical challenge of environmental sensitivity in industrial fermentation by harnessing Xinjiang’s extremophilic microbial resources. Xinjiang's diverse environment has fostered highly tolerant bacterial communities, whose natural plasmids encode evolutionarily shaped stress-resistance mechanisms. By isolating and sequencing these plasmids, our team identifies functional gene elements—such as tolerance to extreme pH levels—to construct standardized expression modules for industrial strains. Integrating nature's evolutionary solutions into bioreactor frameworks, the SILK project aims to enhance fermentation stability, reduce energy consumption for environmental control, and expand the synthetic biology toolkit for extreme environments—transforming Xinjiang's “microbial silk” into industrial resilience.
igem_Munich_2025: Tattoos have long served as markers of identity and belonging. InkSight repurposes this historical medium for modern medicine as a platform comprising engineered mammalian cells encapsulated in a hydrogel matrix for intradermal delivery as a tattoo. This system enables the real-time, equipment-free detection of circulating biomarkers through direct interrogation of the interstitial fluid. The engineered cells express a Modular Extracellular Sensor Architecture (MESA) for target recognition, which triggers one of three engineered contrast-change mechanisms: expression, assembly, or agglomeration. This response is driven by synthetic melanin-producing compartments, specifically encapsulin nanocages that house tyrosinase to enable localized and safe melanin production, resulting in a visible shift in tattoo contrast. InkSight constitutes, to our knowledge, the first paradigm for a continuous, cell-based tattoo biosensor with a visible output, establishing a foundational platform for decentralized diagnostics and personalized medicine.
igem_AFCM-Egypt_2025: Asthma is a very common respiratory disease, its severe form is often characterized by uncontrolled or corticosteroid-resistant inflammation. To overcome this, we developed PRESS, a modular therapeutic platform combining a probiotic delivery system (Lactobacillus plantarum) with an siRNA-based silencing tool (CO-BERA) targeting the inflammatory alarmin TSLP mRNA. Our engineered L. plantarum senses airway inflammation through dual inputs (Hydrogen peroxide and acidic pH) and, upon activation, synthesizes CO-BERA to silence TSLP and suppress downstream inflammatory pathways. For efficient administration, we designed a dry-powder inhalation system, optimized by computational fluid dynamics and validated for aerosol behavior and bacterial viability. PRESS adapted multi-layered biosafety measures, including a toxin–antitoxin kill switch to ensure containment. Reinforced by modeling-guided design and educational outreach with achieving eight UN SDGs. PRESS showcasing how engineered probiotics can function as living inhalable therapeutics, providing a safe, sustainable, and targeted solution for asthma and other inflammatory lung diseases.
igem_HKUST_2025: Cadmium is a severe heavy metal pollutant in several regions. Its effect as a pollutant threatens food safety, notably causing 14-17% of global cropland to be affected. Among sources of cadmium pollution, sludge is particularly detrimental with exacerbated consequences from downstream damage to human health and ecosystems. Within the sludge, there only exists trace yet still harmful concentrations of sludge, causing general heavy metal remediation methods to be ineffective against it. Simultaneously, it is the most significant ecological risk amongst heavy metals. Our team targets sludge and removes the pollutant cadmium by engineering Pseudomonas putida to express metallothioneins on its surface. Our team has introduced this metallothionein to the iGEM Registry and characterized it through Wet Lab Data and Dry Lab modeling. Supported by extensive Human Practices work, our team hopes to demonstrate the potential of our work and it as a promising and sustainable heavy metal bioremediation method.
igem_LZU-China_2025: Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (hUC-MSC)-derived exosomes can ameliorate liver disease via their diverse effector cargo. While individual miRNAs like miR-455-3p and miR-148a-5p are known anti-fibrotic agents, their therapeutic synergy is uninvestigated. This study co-delivers two distinct exosome populations, each artificially supplemented with one of these miRNAs, to assess their combined efficacy.
igem_USP-Brazil_2025: N-glycosylation, the attachment of glycans to asparagine residues, is a critical post-translational modification that influences protein folding, stability, signaling, and activity. Over half of human proteins are glycosylated, yet current therapeutic glycoprotein production depends on eukaryotic hosts, as common models such as Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Escherichia coli are unsuitable. E. coli lacks an N-glycosylation pathway, leading to insoluble proteins, while S. cerevisiae produces hypermannose glycans that are immunogenic in humans. To overcome these limitations, we are engineering optimized microbial platforms for glycoprotein synthesis. In yeast, glycan chain extension is disrupted to generate simpler structures, and in E. coli, a de novo glycosylation system is reconstructed using modular Golden Gate-compatible parts. Both systems aim to produce the universal precursor Man₃GlcNAc₂. We developed 24 yeast mutants to evaluate growth, fitness, morphology, protein production, and glycan transfer, and incorporated archaeal oligosaccharyltransferases into E.coli to explore their ability to transfer glycans to human-like sequons.
igem_XMU-China_2025: In our CRUSTA project, we designed and developed an innovative COS-based bio-preservation technology using principles of synthetic biology. This technology provides a green and efficient alternative to traditional chemical preservatives in the food industry. In our project, we achieved chitosan degradation via a secretion system, enhancing the antibacterial performance of the degradation products by 7.96-fold compared to the wild-type. This project not only has the potential to propel technological innovation and catalyze industrial advancement in food preservation but also aims to introduce advanced concepts of synthetic biology and eco-friendly preservation. These initiatives are expected to improve preservation efficiency, elevate food safety standards, and enhance environmental sustainability, thus bolstering market competitiveness and fostering the sustainable growth of the green food industry and the circular economy.
igem_LZU_2025: As an ancient art form, murals possess significant historical and artistic value. However, factors such as climate change and human activities frequently lead to microbial outbreaks on mural surfaces, resulting in issues such as discoloration of mineral pigments, powdering and flaking of painted layers, and organic staining, which severely threaten their preservation. We have developed a microbial platform capable of producing antimicrobial peptides to inhibit the growth of fungi and bacteria, as well as generating enzymes to degrade organic pigments including melanin and carotenoids. This platform utilizes a pH-inducible switch to transcribe different products under varying pH conditions and incorporates a toggle-switch-based containment mechanism to ensure that our engineered bacteria survive only under specific conditions, thereby preventing environmental release.
igem_LYON_2025: Forever chemicals, or PFAS, are synthetic compounds composed of carbon–fluorine bonds that are nearly impossible to break down. First produced in the 1940s for their exceptional stability and resistance, they are now ubiquitous—in cookware, textiles, and firefighting foams—leading to their accumulation in the environment and human bodies. Long-term exposure has been linked to cancer, hormonal disruption, and immune dysfunction. Yet, no scalable, low-energy solutions currently exist for PFAS degradation. FluoroBreaker aims to address this challenge through two complementary strategies targeting PFOA and TFA. First, we used an AI-assisted bioinformatics docking approach to identify key mutations in a dehalogenase enzyme to enhance TFA degradation. Second, we engineered reporter bacteria carrying a promoter responsive to PFOA, enabling fast, user-friendly detection of PFAS in water. Together, these innovations pave the way for a sustainable, biotechnology-driven response to the PFAS pollution crisis.
igem_Shanghaitech-China_2025: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a widespread yet underestimated disease that causes severe discomfort and lacks effective clinical solutions. To address challenges in early diagnosis and precise treatment, we focused on Granzyme K (GZMK), a key enzyme driving CRS progression. Centered on this target, we established an integrated diagnostic–therapeutic framework. A colloidal-gold rapid test strip enables early and accessible detection, while small-molecule inhibitors achieve precise enzymatic inhibition and inflammation control. In parallel, we developed two supporting technology platforms: Prometheus, for de novo protein design, and Nexus, for high-throughput affinity measurement. They enable efficient design and validation of high-affinity protein binders, contributing more powerful research tools to the field of synthetic biology.
igem_Oxford_2025: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a silent pandemic claiming millions of lives each year as more pathogens evade existing treatments. CASPER (cell-based antimicrobial screening and programmable elimination response) offers an integrated platform that unites diagnostics and therapeutics into a single, accessible system. The diagnostic module overcomes limitations of PCR and lateral flow assays by using a two-step reaction that screens for bacterial presence and produces a clear color change as a visible output. This enables rapid, broad-range, and equipment-free detection suitable for low-resource settings. The therapeutic module introduces programmable mini cells and extracellular vesicles as DNA delivery shuttles capable of selectively recognizing bacterial targets and triggering cell death from within. By combining detection and response, CASPER provides a scalable and affordable solution to antimicrobial resistance with the potential to transform infection control and save millions of lives worldwide.
igem_McGill_2025: One of nature’s greatest feats is multicellularity—joining together single cells into a whole that is greater than the sum of its parts. Cohera is a complete toolkit for multicellular engineering, allowing synthetic biologists to access the full potential of cell-cell adhesion. Our system enables the creation of microbial networks that can be formed and dissolved on command using a collection of membrane-displayed proteins. Our Model, CoheraTune, expands the range of environments in which our tool operates by strengthening the core of our project at the molecular level. At the macroscopic level, bioengineers can leverage Cohera to solve problems in diverse fields. To facilitate the use of our system as a foundational tool, we developed human-centred roadmaps for applications spanning all iGEM plazas. Cohera streamlines the process of engineering cell-cell adhesion, unlocking endless possibilities.
igem_UNICAMP-Brazil_2025: Orange production faces severe losses caused by Greening, Green Mold and Sour Rot, threatening food security and vitamin C availability. Especially in Brazil, leader of orange juice and fruit production, this directly affects livelihoods. To tackle this challenge, we focused on CTX, an antimicrobial peptide from Brazilian Cerrado biodiversity, and engineered three different hosts: E. coli, S. cerevisiae, and A. oryzae to optimize its production through coupling-strategies. To guide CTX application, we developed a mathematical model simulating Greening progression in the phloem and designed Sniffer, a hardware device combining an electronic nose and machine learning for rapid field diagnosis. Performing economic analysis to assess industrial scalability of approaches we demonstrated cost-effectiveness through solid-state fermentation using orange peels residues. Thus, Pepcitrus bridges laboratory innovation and real-world application, incorporating different perspectives from farmers, industry, and society to save oranges.
igem_Hamburg_2025: 90% of mushroom poisonings are caused by α-amanitin, one of the deadliest mushroom toxins which can be found in the death cap mushroom. Just half a mushroom can be fatal, as the toxin inhibits RNA Polymerase II, blocking protein production and causing severe organ damage, especially to the liver and kidneys. Although treatments exist, there is no specific antidote yet. Our iGEM project, DeathCapTrap, aims to develop a modular nanobody-based antidote to neutralize α-amanitin in the bloodstream and protect liver cells. In the WetLab, we established a pipeline to produce a nuclear-targeted nanobody in E. coli. We also explored lipid nanoparticles for delivery and designed a testing protocol with liver cell models. In the DryLab, AI tools helped us design toxin-binding proteins. Our goal is to create a life-saving therapy and a versatile platform to fight intracellular toxins, while raising awareness of the dangers of mushroom poisoning.
igem_LZU-MEDICINE-CHINA_2025: This project aims to develop an intelligent engineered bacterium for the precise treatment of perioperative gut microbiota dysbiosis. Using the safe Lactobacillus casei as the chassis, we have integrated a multifunctional genetic circuit. First, by introducing the accA and OLE1 genes, the engineered bacterium can synthesize and release oleic acid—beneficial for gut barrier repair—under the specific regulation of the bile salt-responsive promoter P16090. Simultaneously, the bacterium expresses the antimicrobial peptide defensin DEFB4A to precisely suppress opportunistic pathogens. To ensure biosafety, we designed a bile salt-responsive Hok/Sok toxin-antitoxin "kill switch" system, controlled by the same P16090 promoter. This mechanism ensures that the engineered bacterium only colonizes the gut; any leakage into the external environment triggers its automatic clearance. Together, this living therapeutic platform is equipped with functions for barrier repair, pathogen suppression, and self-regulation, setting a new standard for targeted, safe, and intelligent interventions.
igem_ULethbridge_2025: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is a biomolecule widely utilized in healthcare and cosmetic applications. Traditionally, HA is extracted from animal or bacterial sources. Research has examined the potential of microbial production using non-pathogenic bacteria. These methods could be a promising ethical and scalable alternative. Given current demand, HA yields remain insufficient.  We aim to maximize production efficiency through Multiplex Automated Genome Engineering (MAGE) and specialized E. coli. MAGE enables rapid, high-throughput modification of multiple genomic sites simultaneously, facilitating metabolic pathway optimization and synthetic biology applications. However, MAGE is hindered by high cost, complexity, and limited versatility of existing hardware. Our group is developing the Open-Source Automated Genome Engineering (O-SAGE) platform, leveraging affordable, commercially available components and open-source parts. The goal is to engineer E. coli capable of efficient HA production using O-SAGE, providing a safe, ethical, and scalable source of HA while also democratizing access to advanced genome engineering technologies.
igem_JLU-NBBMS_2025: Ginsenoside Ro is one of the rarest and most valuable bioactive compounds in ginseng, celebrated for its potent antioxidant properties and multi-target therapeutic potential. However, its natural abundance is extremely low, and traditional extraction methods are both costly and environmentally unsustainable. To address this challenge, we engineered a recombinant Saccharomyces cerevisiae system capable of converting waste oil–derived carbon sources, such as glycerol and fatty acids, into Ro through an optimized three-step biosynthetic pathway. By integrating metabolic engineering, enzyme evolution, and modeling-guided optimization, we achieved a substantial enhancement in Ro yield while reducing resource consumption and environmental footprint. This platform exemplifies the principles of a circular bioeconomy, transforming industrial waste into high-value pharmaceuticals. Combining strong environmental benefits with significant economic potential, our work establishes a scalable, sustainable model for advancing green manufacturing and the future of synthetic biology–based healthcare.
igem_BUCT_2025: Polyester plastics (PET/PBAT/PLA) persist in marine environments and form harmful microplastics. To tackle source-level persistence and end-of-pipe remediation we combined marine-enzyme discovery, computational protein redesign and AI-driven mutation design, inorganic CaCO₃–SiO₂ immobilization compatible with melt processing, and an E. coli dual-anchor surface-display (adhesion + SpyTag/SpyCatcher-tethered hydrolase). A marine hydrolase (“2013”) was mined, characterized and redesigned to a soluble active variant (SEQ4); immobilization conferred thermal robustness with ≈40% activity retained after brief high-temperature treatment, supporting processing compatibility. Enzyme-containing films exhibited accelerated surface erosion in 28-day real-seawater assays; the dual-anchor strain enhanced local TPA release versus controls; and a rapid hydroxylation–Fenton fluorescence assay enabled sensitive TPA quantification. Future work will optimize kinetics for high-crystallinity PET, scale immobilization/compounding to pilot, integrate a genetically encoded TPA biosensor, and assess environmental fate, safety and regulatory pathways.
igem_JLU-CP_2025: Tuneable Dream Drive: To address sleep disorders caused by circadian rhythm disruption during space missions, the JLU-CP team engineered a multi-layer regulatory melatonin synthesis system using Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) as a chassis. This system integrates a red-light-controlled genetic circuit with the serine recombinase Bxb1, enabling reversible promoter inversion to switch between serotonin production and melatonin biosynthesis. A pharmacokinetic (PK) model optimized dosage under simulated microgravity, while deep-learning-driven enzyme engineering enhanced HsAANAT catalytic efficiency. We then built an expression model to predict melatonin yield under light conditions for controllable production. For biosafety, the design includes a hypoxia-activated toxin–antitoxin module and tryptophan-auxotrophic safeguard. Additionally, we developed iTutor, the most inclusive-iGEM LLM trained on iGEM Wiki, PubMed, and arXiv data, provides real-time computational and experimental guidance. This engineered probiotic functions as a gut-colonizing “biological clock calibrator,” enabling precise, red-light-induced melatonin release to support astronauts’ circadian health during spaceflight.
igem_DTU-Denmark_2025: Fast fashion has accelerated the accumulation of synthetic textile waste, with nylon being among the least recycled fractions. Landfilling and incineration are the current disposal methods, producing microplastics and emitting greenhouse gases. NomNomNylon proposes a bio-upcycling strategy that couples enzymatic pretreatment with microbial valorisation. To enhance depolymerization, we developed a protein engineering pipeline to increase thermostability and activity while exploring nature’s enzymatic diversity through sequence mining. These variants and homologues were tested in vitro using a cell-free assay on raw nylon. We employed a bioengineered Pseudomonas putida strain to metabolise nylon-derived oligomers and channel carbon flux toward indigoidine, a sustainable alternative to petrochemical indigo. Beyond lab work, we integrated feedback from experts, policymakers, and NGOs, and raised awareness among the public and youth through educational initiatives. We have shown that nylon waste can serve as a valuable feedstock for high-value products, contributing to a greener textile future.
igem_HUST-China_2025: Squoilene tackles waste oil (WO) pollution and the high cost of squalene production by integrating experimental work, model and hardware into a cohesive synthetic biology project, engineering Yarrowia lipolytica into an efficient cellular refinery.Through human practice and interdisciplinary communication, we refined design and promoted implementation.
